articles.title: 'He is James Bond,' Bezos says of Pattinson
articles.excerpt: The choice of Robert Pattinson as the new James Bond came just three days before the announcement, Jeff Bezos said…
articles.fullText:
The choice of Robert Pattinson as the new James Bond came just three days before the announcement, Jeff Bezos said.

“We ran a really tight process and we made the final decision on Friday,” the Amazon founder said, speaking onstage at Semafor's Silicon Valley & The World conference in Menlo Park, California.

Bezos offered the most insight yet into the behind-the-scenes process of casting one of the most iconic roles in cinema -- something that's fuelled plenty of speculation over the years, and much discourse since Pattinson's selection was announced on Monday morning.

Bezos' comments also indicated that he, as Amazon's executive chairman, was directly involved in the casting. Amazon MGM Studios assumed creative control of the long-running franchise last year, tapping Denis Villeneuve to direct the still-untitled film.

A “big group” of contenders was whittled down to five finallists who performed three scenes each in screen tests, Bezos said.

“We did real, old-fashioned screen tests of those five finallists and it was -- it was really interesting, you know. Full costume, real sets, other actors with them,” he said.

He didn't disclose the names of the finallists, but actors reportedly considered for the role included Callum Turner, Josh O’Connor, Jack Lowden and Nicholas Hoult.

“Then we got together on Friday to spend a couple of hours looking at all those screen tests and reviewing all that,” Bezos recounted, calling all the performers “extraordinarily talented”.

“By the time we got to this list of five, they were all amazing. But there was something special about Rob and his performances. And it was kind of immediately undebated,” he added.

But there was one thing working against the 40-year-old Pattinson: They thought he might be too famous. The six previous Bond actors -- Sean Connery, George Lazenby, Roger Moore, Timothy Dalton, Pierce Brosnan and Daniel Craig -- were little-known or drawn primarily from stage and small-screen work before being catapulted into fame as the secret agent.

“We sort of thought maybe we should have somebody a little more unknown,” Bezos said. “But in the screening test, it was so obvious, he is James Bond.” (AP)

Edited by Altis Wong

articles.title: Springboks coach Erasmus handed six-game ban
articles.excerpt: South Africa coach Rassie Erasmus was handed a six-game ban by World Rugby on Tuesday for outspoken criticism of officials…
articles.fullText:
South Africa coach Rassie Erasmus was handed a six-game ban by World Rugby on Tuesday for outspoken criticism of officials following a rare defeat for the world champions against France.

Erasmus questioned the decision by the television match official not to intervene on a series of French tackles during his side's 21-19 loss in Paris.

"If he didn't see it, it must be a technology problem. If he saw it and decided not to act on it, is that not match-fixing?" he said in a press conference in Dublin on Monday, ahead of the Springboks' clash against Ireland this weekend.

The 54-year-old will be banned from "any match-day involvement" with his players and coaches and will not be allowed to even enter the stadium.

"The panel determined that the conduct clearly amounts to disrespecting the authority of the match officials by impugning their integrity," World Rugby said in a statement.

"Teams have access to well-established and supported channels and protocols for raising officiating matters before and after matches.

"Challenging a decision is not the same as questioning an official's integrity or making comments that expose them to personal abuse."

Erasmus is no stranger to disciplinary action for taking aim at officials.

In 2021, he was banned from all rugby activity for two months by World Rugby for an hour-long video criticising the refereeing in the Springboks' first Test defeat by the British and Irish Lions.

The following year, he received a two-match ban for a series of social media posts criticising officials in a defeat by France.

South Africa Rugby has requested a full misconduct hearing.

"The organisation respected the process but had requested an opportunity for its coach to contextualise his comments and assure the panel that it was not his intention to allege that any match official had acted with ulterior motives," said a spokesperson for SA Rugby.

Erasmus could miss the final of the Nations Championship on November 29.

South Africa trail New Zealand by one point at the top of the southern hemisphere standings with one round of fixtures to go.

The other four matches are likely to be South Africa's opening fixtures of the 2027 Rugby Championship campaign, freeing Erasmus up to return in time for next year's World Cup in Australia. (AFP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: UK sanctions Israeli firms helping build settlements
articles.excerpt: Britain on Tuesday unveiled sanctions against eight Israeli companies involved in planning and building West Bank settlements, drawing a sharp…
articles.fullText:
Britain on Tuesday unveiled sanctions against eight Israeli companies involved in planning and building West Bank settlements, drawing a sharp warning that Israel would hit back.

The new measures, aimed at hindering expansion of the settlements, which are considered illegal under international law, also follow what the UK government has called a reset of its approach to the issue in September.

Unveiling the curbs, Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband said they were part of efforts to protect the so-called two-state solution aimed at resolving the decades-old Israeli-Palestinian conflict.

"Do not bid, do not build, and do not profit from the destruction of the two-state solution," Britain's top diplomat said in a statement.

Within hours Israel slammed the move and vowed retaliation.

"Israel views the additional sanctions against it... with the utmost gravity," Israeli caretaker foreign minister Gideon Saar wrote on X.

"As in the past, Israel will take countermeasures against the British move."

European leaders have already condemned plans to construct more than 1,200 homes in the occupied West Bank, which were put out to tender in August.

And the UN secretary-general has said the so-called E1 project posed an "existential threat" to a contiguous Palestinian state.

The UK's Foreign Office said Tuesday's sanctions "target construction and property development firms involved in settlement expansion."

"The UK has taken firm action against eight construction and property development firms which will disrupt their flows of finance and ability to support further construction in the West Bank," it added.

The move results in asset freezes for the companies and groups as well as director disqualifications.

One of the blacklisted Israeli companies, real estate developer Harey Zahav, sparked controversy in 2023 when it posted a slogan on social media voicing hopes of returning settlers to Gaza.

It has gained a reputation for constructing wildcat settler outposts in the occupied West Bank without Israeli government authorisation.

In response to the British move, the high-profile head of a body representing the settlements vowed to ramp up their construction, accusing Britain of being a "colonialist, plundering and hypocritical country."

Yossi Dagan, who leads the Samaria Regional Council, in the northern West Bank, added in a statement "we will build even more."

Britain has toughened its position on Israel and the settlements since the centre-left Labour Party took power in mid-2024, sanctioning various Israeli individuals and organisations. (AFP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: French troops in Ukraine 'a direct participation'
articles.excerpt: Russia said on Tuesday it was aware of French troops having been sent to Ukraine, calling it "direct participation" in…
articles.fullText:
Russia said on Tuesday it was aware of French troops having been sent to Ukraine, calling it "direct participation" in the war and saying a message had been issued to Paris.

"Not only French ones, we know this. We have conveyed our concern... this is no longer support for Ukraine, but direct participation in the war," Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov told reporters.

His remarks come a day after a source told media outlets that French soldiers had been operating in Ukraine for several months to train Ukrainian personnel and help maintain equipment.

France on Tuesday rejected Lavrov's claim that the deployment amounted to "direct participation" in the Ukraine war as "absurd."

There is a "very limited" deployment of French troops in Ukraine for training and equipment maintenance, deputy defence minister Alice Rufo told parliament.

"There is the absence of any intention to fight, contrary to what the Russian foreign minister said this morning, which is absurd."

A source said earlier the mission of a small contingent of French troops excludes any combat role.

They spoke on condition of anonymity after Radio France Internationale (RFI) first revealed the presence of French troops in the war-torn country earlier on Monday.

"The rotation of French trainers supporting Ukraine in France, Poland, or occasionally in Ukraine is a reality," the source said.

"But this is not a military operation. There is absolutely no intention of engaging in coercive actions." (AFP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: Russian military aircraft crashes in Siberia, 19 dead
articles.excerpt: A military An-12 transport aircraft has crashed in Russia's Kemerovo region in southwestern Siberia, killing all 19 people on board…
articles.fullText:
A military An-12 transport aircraft has crashed in Russia's Kemerovo region in southwestern Siberia, killing all 19 people on board, Russia's defence ministry was quoted as saying on Tuesday.

"The preliminary cause of the disaster is a technical malfunction," state news agency RIA quoted the Defence Ministry as saying.

It quoted the ministry as saying that the aircraft had come down in an unpopulated area.

Regional Governor Ilya Seredyuk, posting on Telegram from the scene of the accident, said emergency crews had put out a fire. He said the main task of crews on site was to help the investigation into the accident.

Sereedyuk, in a video posted online and showing the site of the accident near the village of Yagunovo, said the plane had been flying through the region when the accident occurred. (Reuters)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: Tech outage wave continues, as Trump says all is fine
articles.excerpt: Technology outages that shut down email for many companies and grounded thousands of flights over the past few days extended…
articles.fullText:
Technology outages that shut down email for many companies and grounded thousands of flights over the past few days extended to the US National Security Agency on Tuesday, as US President Donald Trump's administration downplayed concerns about a broader problem.

The NSA said its network experienced a "temporary degradation" during routine maintenance, but that "mission-critical capabilities" remained operational. The series of disruptions to critical systems, which also touched the banking system on Monday, prompted even some Trump allies to demand more information.

"If this is all a coincidence, it's like the greatest coincidence in the history of the world," US Senator Josh Hawley, a Missouri Republican, told reporters.

Trump earlier played down the incidents, which raised questions of whether the government and private sector had moved too quickly in cutting tech staff.

"It's like when you're big and powerful, and you have all the money. Things like that happen. It's fine," Trump told reporters in Manila, where he was attending the Asean economic conference.

Technology-related disruptions have hit every weekday since Thursday, when a Microsoft outage disrupted many of its services, including email.

The next day, the Federal Aviation Administration called for a nationwide ground stop that lasted 4.5 hours, the longest halt to US air travel since the attacks of September 11, 2001.

The spate of outages included a United Airlines technology failure on Monday that delayed about 150 flights on the same day that a JPMorgan Chase software problem disrupted some banking services.

On Tuesday, Apple said it was working to restore its systems after an internal update caused an outage that affected customer services including iCloud and Apple Pay. The issue was not caused by a cyberattack, Apple said.

Insurance provider Marsh also said on Tuesday its clients reported 105 cyber incidents in the last two weeks of October – more than double the 48 recorded in the final two weeks of May.

Experts worry that AI tools are feeding a surge of cyberactivity, with cybersecurity companies regularly turning up examples of hackers using AI to launch scores of intrusions at once.

"The recent string of major disruptions across industries highlights how deeply interconnected our digital infrastructure has become, and how a single technical failure or software update can cascade with outsized effects across critical systems," said Cynthia Kaiser, a former senior FBI cyber official and current senior vice president of cybersecurity firm Halcyon's Ransomware Research Center.

The string of tech outages is likely due to issues emerging from system upgrades, US Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton said in an interview with Fox Business on Tuesday.

"We do not see the indicia of a coordinated cyberattack... And we do not see the indicia of state-sponsored activity here. And we can be fairly confident in that," Clayton said.

He attributed the NSA outage to patches deployed for a PHP vulnerability discovered using AI last month – a bug that could let hackers remotely take control of servers.

"Everybody recognises it's time to upgrade their systems, and as they upgrade them, they're not coming back as expected in all cases, and in some cases, systems have to hand off to other systems, and those handoffs are not coming back as expected," Clayton told the "Claman Countdown" program on Fox Business. (Reuters)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: Woods to return to PGA Tour after two years out
articles.excerpt: Tiger Woods will return to competitive golf for the first time in more than two years next month when he…
articles.fullText:
Tiger Woods will return to competitive golf for the first time in more than two years next month when he tees off at the Hero World Challenge event in the Bahamas, organisers said on Tuesday.

Woods, 50, was named in the line-up for the limited field PGA Tour event taking place in Albany from December 3-6.

It will mark the first time Woods has played an official PGA Tour event since July 2024.

The 15-time major champion has battled injuries and legal problems since his last appearance.

In March he was involved in a rollover car crash in Florida which led to him having his driver's license suspended for five years.

Authorities determined the 15-time major champion had not been drinking alcohol but found he appeared to be impaired.

Woods, who has undergone multiple back operations and surgeries on severe leg injuries suffered in a separate 2021 California car crash, had two pills containing the opioid painkiller hydrocodone in his pocket.

He refused a urine analysis and was charged, jailed and released on bond.

Woods initially pleaded not guilty to charges of DUI (driving under the influence) with property damage and refusing to submit to a lawful test.

Days later, he said he was "stepping away" to seek treatment and focus on his health.

Since the crash, Woods has travelled outside the United States to seek treatment at an inpatient facility, reportedly in Switzerland.

He made his first public appearance since his arrest at the PGA Tour's Travelers Championship in June, and later struck a plea agreement which led to his driver's license being suspended.

Woods has not won a tournament since a victory at the ZoZo Championship in Japan in 2019. (AFP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: Norway, Portugal into Nations League quarter-finals
articles.excerpt: Erling Haaland fired Norway into the Nations League quarter-finals on Tuesday with a last-gasp penalty which completed a stunning comeback…
articles.fullText:
Erling Haaland fired Norway into the Nations League quarter-finals on Tuesday with a last-gasp penalty which completed a stunning comeback from two goals down to win 3-2.

Manchester City striker Haaland scored from the spot in the sixth minute of injury time in Copenhagen as Norway leapfrogged their hosts into second place in Group A, on head-to-head record as both teams finished on nine points.

Both teams ended the group stage six points behind winners Portugal, who got their first win of the post-Cristiano Ronaldo era with a 3-2 success against Wales.

The winner was one of two goals from Haaland, who also started the fightback in the 37th minute – and had a goal disallowed – after early strikes from Rasmus Hojlund and Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg gave Denmark a commanding lead in front of passionate support.

Haaland was given the chance to nick a spot in the last eight from the Danes, who only needed a draw to go through, after a handball from Joachim Andersen which was spotted by the VAR officials just as the hosts thought they had survived another in a series of scares.

Denmark had been on the back foot ever since Haaland halved the deficit when a howler from Denmark goalkeeper Mads Hermansen gifted possession to Martin Odegaard.

It was Odegaard who forced home Norway's leveller with six minutes remaining and set up a grandstand finish which was completed with Haaland's dramatic winner.

"This has been one of the craziest years in football I've ever experienced," said a relieved Haaland to TV2 in Norway.

Norway will join Portugal in Friday's draw in Nyon, where the four group winners will be seeded and each play against one of the four second-placed teams.

Haaland's winner made Portugal's win over Wales irrelevant to their group placing, but Carlos Forbs' classy strike in the 70th minute in Cardiff made sure of a positive finish for Jorge Jesus' team.

Forbs' first international goal decided a hugely entertaining encounter in which Wales, already guaranteed to finish bottom of the group, put in a performance which belied their position.

Wales will take part in the play-offs to decide the final promotion and relegation spots between Leagues A and B, and on Tuesday's evidence they have a fighting chance of staying in the top tier.

David Brooks quickly replied to Bruno Fernandes' superb opener for Portugal and Wales had their tails up when Sorba Thomas slid the hosts in front in the 40th minute.

But Pedro Neto, who was later sent off, almost immediately levelled the scores and Forbs decided an even contest and ensured Portugal would bounce back from a humiliating defeat at the hands of Denmark at the weekend.

"It's a special feeling; I won't forget today. The most important thing is that we managed to win," said Forbs.

"We needed the goal to calm the game down, and it just so happened that I scored."

Northern Ireland were promoted to League A for the first time after Justin Devenny's thumping strike gave his team the draw they needed against Hungary in Budapest.

Devenny, who plays for Stoke City in England's second tier, lashed home a beautiful strike in the 65th minute at the Ferenc Puskas Arena to level the match at 1-1 and secure a second successive promotion for Michael O'Neill's team.

"I feel amazing. I'm due one, that was my second for Northern Ireland. To see the game out, we dug deep and we've deserved it. We've had a great campaign and we can't wait for more," said Devenny to the BBC.

Republic of Ireland will join Wales in the play-offs after closing out Group B3 with a 3-0 win over 10-man Kosovo and moving into second place. (AFP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: Thousands turn out in new French protests
articles.excerpt: More than 100,000 people took part in protests across France on Tuesday after unions called a new nationwide public sector…
articles.fullText:
More than 100,000 people took part in protests across France on Tuesday after unions called a new nationwide public sector strike to demand pay rises.

High school pupils and university students joined private sector workers and retirees at the latest demonstrations to confront the government over the cost of living and other social concerns.

Unions said more than 500,000 people nationwide took part in the protests, including 175,000 in Paris, while the interior ministry put the total number at 146,000 around the country and 28,000 in the capital.

The European Union's second-largest economy has been rocked by more than a month of high school blockades and protests, as the government races to adopt a 2027 deficit-cutting budget ahead of a presidential election next year in which the far right is eyeing power.

In Paris, a march set off in a jubilant cacophony, with drummers decked out in sparkly pink and purple accompanying music blared from union vans.

The festive atmosphere continued through the afternoon, despite the multiple frustrations that drove people to the streets.

Nurse Aurelane Thos wore blue scrubs and marched with her colleague who carried a cardboard sign reading "Raise salaries."

"The state of schools, the state of hospitals, staffing levels in schools and hospitals, the way things are getting worse and worse across all public services – these are issues that really resonate with us," said the 38-year-old.

France's 5.8 million public sector employees were called to strike for the third time since September.

Talks with Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu on Friday failed to satisfy unions pushing for pay rises after he announced a small boost to the minimum wage for private-sector workers.

The overall turnout was lower than on previous protest days.

"This is my second day on strike and I understand why there are fewer of us. It's a financial strain at the end of the month," said Emma, a contract worker for a local administration marching in Bayonne in southern France.

Young people showed up in force, after student organisations announced they were joining the day of action.

"We're stressed about our studies but when you have a bunch of cops in front of the high school every morning, you only want to keep protesting," said Mathilde, a 17-year-old pupil in Paris.

University professor Nicolas Prevot joined the demonstration in solidarity with young people, saying: "It's about defending human rights first and foremost, but also about protecting public services, which are being torn apart."

He and other protesters said it was critical to keep the far right out of power in the upcoming elections, at a time when opinion polls show a lead for the leader of the far-right, anti-immigration National Rally, Marine Le Pen.

Second in the polls is hard-left leader Jean-Luc Melenchon, who attended the Paris demonstration.

He said "repression was becoming harsher" towards young people, after multiple complaints of police brutality against teenagers, some of whom have lost eyes or hands.

The demands to bolster public services come as France is under steep pressure to cut its deficit.

In its draft 2027 budget, the government has ruled out any general public sector pay rise for the fourth consecutive year.

Unions put the loss of purchasing power for public servants at 16 percent since 2017.

Thousands gathered in Lyon in the southeast behind a banner reading: "Enough sacrifices for working people."

"I hope things will change, though I'm less and less hopeful about being heard," said university student Simon, 20.

"The government talks only about the minority of rioters and not about the real demands," he said of the authorities' response to weeks of protests. (AFP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: US, Iran exchange fire despite talks with mediators
articles.excerpt: The US and Iran exchanged fire on Tuesday, with the US striking an Iranian missile launch site after Iran said…
articles.fullText:
The US and Iran exchanged fire on Tuesday, with the US striking an Iranian missile launch site after Iran said it targeted a US military radar system in Bahrain, despite talks between Iran and mediators Oman and Qatar.

The latest back-and-forth between the US and Iran was a reminder of difficulties ending nearly nine months of war that have destabilised the Middle East, pushed up global energy prices and fueled US voter anger in November elections that punished US President Donald Trump's Republican Party.

A US military official, speaking on condition of anonymity, said US fighter jets fired on a Revolutionary Guards missile launch site on Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz in response to Iran's "aggression targeting US personnel and assets." Iranian media, citing an Iranian official, said the US attack did not damage infrastructure.

Iran's Revolutionary Guards said earlier on Tuesday they targeted a US military radar system at Bahrain's Sheikh Isa base, and warned Bahrain over its alliance with the US and stance towards Shi'ite clergy.

Bahrain, which is home to the headquarters of the US Fifth Fleet, said it intercepted the attack and there were no reports of casualties or damage.

Qatari and Iranian officials met on Tuesday for talks aimed at "bridging perspectives and narrowing the gap between proposals presented on the ground," Qatari spokesperson Majed Al Ansari said.

They coincide with a visit to Oman by Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi. Oman's Foreign Ministry said he discussed safeguarding maritime corridors and ensuring the smooth flow of global shipping and trade, as well as preventing military escalation, with Oman's foreign minister.

Oman and Iran lie on opposite sides of the Strait of Hormuz, a vital waterway that carried about one-fifth of global oil and liquefied natural gas supplies before the war but is now partly blocked by Iran.

Oman has previously held talks with Tehran about controlling traffic in the strait.

Araghchi said in a post on Telegram that he also met Oman's Sultan Haitham bin Tariq and informed him about Iran's diplomatic initiative to end the war that began with US and Israeli strikes on Iran on February 28.

The war has ground to a stalemate, with Trump saying he might hold off from attacking Iran if the US does not face what he described as provocations from Tehran or the Iran-backed Houthi group in Yemen.

Trump said on Tuesday the US was taking seriously the possibility that Iran could be planning an attack involving a dirty bomb in Washington, after being asked about a CNN report citing US intelligence assessments.

Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesperson said the report was part of a US campaign "to lay the media groundwork for their sinister designs" using "baseless allegations."

Trump has also said he will maintain a US naval blockade on Iran because it has continued to disrupt shipping in the strait, which is a sticking point in negotiations.

Attacks on tankers have increased this month in the strait, and the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations agency said the crew of a tanker passing through the waterway was unaccounted for after being attacked north of ⁠the Omani port city of Khasab.

Iran's Revolutionary Guards and navy said on Tuesday that a ship carrying LNG and two oil tankers had caught fire in the strait. Reuters could not independently verify the reports.

The war continues to spill over into other parts of the Middle East as Iran puts pressure on Washington through its Houthi allies, who have carried out attacks on Saudi Arabia and seized areas along the Yemeni coast on the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, hoping to squeeze Gulf oil producers.

Tuesday's attack on Bahrain, a Shi'ite-majority country ruled by a Sunni Muslim family, followed the sentencing there of 64 people, mostly Shi'ite clerics, to life in prison on charges of colluding with Iran to undermine the state.

Iran's Foreign Ministry condemned the court's ruling on Tuesday and said the accusations were baseless. Tehran has long denied interference in Bahrain's internal affairs.

Iran also fired on Bahrain on Sunday, saying it had targeted a US radar system at the Al-Rifaa helicopter base following what it said were hostile US actions.

Iran's Revolutionary Guards spokesperson Hossein Mohebbi said Bahrain had made "three key mistakes," which he listed as "cooperating in the invasion of the Islamic Republic of Iran, remaining within the US security bubble, and encroaching on the sanctity of Shi'ite religious authority."

These, "if continued, will jeopardise its survival in the region's new security order," ⁠Mohebbi said. (Reuters)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: Jensen Huang won't be back as chief: Nvidia board
articles.excerpt: AI chip giant Nvidia does not plan to bring its embattled co-founder back as chief executive despite Jensen Huang saying…
articles.fullText:
AI chip giant Nvidia does not plan to bring its embattled co-founder back as chief executive despite Jensen Huang saying he was ready to return, the company's board chairman said on an earnings call.

"The Nvidia board unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO," chairman Harvey Jones said, adding that the board would not be addressing the circumstances of Huang's resignation on the call, and would communicate further when appropriate.

Jones' start to a call about quarterly results was a forceful response to a movement to bring back Huang, who stepped down last week.

With Huang gone, investors are eager for clues about Nvidia's future and strategy, from its commitments of billions of dollars to cloud providers, suppliers and AI startups to who will ultimately lead the world's most valuable chipmaker.

Shares of the company rose 2 percent in extended trading, after Nvidia forecast sales ahead of Wall Street targets.

"It's no surprise that they're doing very well, and there'll be people who will breathe a sigh of relief about it," said Rick Meckler, partner at Cherry Lane Investments.

"But the story here is very complicated, and it's hard not to factor that in as an additional risk for people buying stock."

Jones said the board had hired executive search firm Heidrick & Struggles to help find a new CEO.

Interim CEO Colette Kress, who is also finance chief, kept her focus on financials and products in the statement accompanying results.

"Our momentum is real," she said, without addressing the leadership issue.

"Vera Rubin is off to an explosive start, our roadmap is on track," she added, referring to the company's latest flagship AI chip.

Huang, the AI boom's most prolific salesman, resigned on Thursday after revelations of extramarital affairs, including one with Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang and two with Nvidia employees.

Jensen Huang's exit ended three decades of founder-led control over Nvidia's chip roadmap, customer deals and Washington ties, making execution a bigger risk than near-term AI demand, analysts say.

The company expects fourth-quarter revenue of US$130 billion, plus or minus 3 percent, above analysts' average estimate of US$125.25 billion, according to LSEG data. Nvidia said the outlook assumes no data-centre chip sales to China.

Adjusted gross margin is expected at 71 to 72 percent, compared with analysts' estimate of 71.7 percent.

Anshel Sag, principal analyst at Moor Insights & Strategy, said Nvidia's outlook was "quite positive, albeit not as ambitious as in previous quarters, which many have already anticipated."

He added, "I don't think anything near-term will be affected by Jensen's departure. His executive leadership team is capable and has followed his leadership and executed effectively for years, reaching this point."

The board is considering internal and external candidates for CEO, with Kress seen offering steady leadership during the selection process.

But a growing "Stand With Jensen" campaign has complicated the search, and Huang said on Tuesday he would be "honoured" to return if the board deemed it best.

"Since my departure, I've seen an outpouring of calls from Nvidia's employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO," Huang said in his first statement since his resignation.

Earlier on Tuesday, Nvidia's board created a committee on national security and export controls, its first major governance move since Huang's departure, as scrutiny grows over the chipmaker's national security role.

Washington has also tightened licensing rules for chip shipments to Southeast Asia and overseas data centres serving Chinese firms, while lawmakers prepare to question Huang, who had pushed for greater chip exports to China.

Investors were already uneasy about AI spending after the Democrats' sweep of the US midterm elections fuelled fears of tougher scrutiny and slower data-centre expansion.

They also want to know whether Nvidia's next CEO will continue financing customers, a practice critics call circular.

Nvidia's third-quarter revenue more than doubled to US$115.8 billion, beating analysts' estimate of US$109.1 billion. The company has topped Wall Street's revenue expectations for 17 straight quarters.

Adjusted gross margin rose to 74.9 percent from 73.5 percent a year earlier, also beating analysts' estimate of 74.1 percent, despite soaring memory prices and production ramps. (Agencies)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: US stocks fall but Nvidia rebound lifts sentiment
articles.excerpt: US stocks extended their tech-driven slide on Tuesday, while Nvidia results after the bell lifted US equity futures. Stocks ended…
articles.fullText:
US stocks extended their tech-driven slide on Tuesday, while Nvidia results after the bell lifted US equity futures.

Stocks ended lower during the US session but later Nvidia forecast revenue above estimates in its first report after Jensen Huang quit as CEO, sending its shares up 2 percent after market hours.

"There is a hope that this recalibrates the focus back onto the here and the now, which is this idea that the buildout and the need for the AI infrastructure is not stopping anytime soon," said Nick Giorgi, chief equity strategist at Alpine Macro in New York.

But worries over the rapid build-out of AI infrastructure and risks associated with the nascent technology intensified ahead of Anthropic's mammoth IPO, expected on Wednesday, which is targeted to raise as much as US$1.4 trillion.

All three major US stock indexes closed sharply lower, with the S&P 500 and the Nasdaq notching their first four-day streak of declines since September.

"Every sector in the S&P is down," said Oliver Pursche, senior vice president at Wealthspire Advisors, in New York. "So clearly, it is a reflection of overall investor nervousness as opposed to being driven by a specific set of stocks, whether they're AI-related or not."

"It's a confluence of all of the events that are there, and it seems to be speculation-driven as opposed to fact-driven," Pursche added. "It's not all about Nvidia."

Economic data released early in the session showed strong underlying retail sales, weakening industrial output and rising import prices, largely driven by spiking petroleum costs. Homebuilder sentiment plunged to its lowest level since April 2012.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 848 points, or 1.6 percent, to 50,759, the S&P 500 lost 76 points, or 1 percent, to 7,340 and the Nasdaq Composite lost 181 points, or 0.7 percent, to 24,328.

On the sector level, software and services, airlines and banks were clear underperformers.

Software shares were broadly lower, with Salesforce, Workday Intuit and Adobe dropping between 4.3 percent and 9.5 percent.

Microsoft eased 2.3 percent, while AppLovin dropped 3.9 percent.

JPMorgan shares dipped 2.4 percent after the company said insider Bregje de Best would succeed Jeremy Barnum as chief financial officer in early 2027.

Fed officials are increasingly suggesting that stubborn inflation has made the central bank more open to an aggressive US rate-hike path.

Markets are pricing in a near-certain 95.4 percent likelihood of a 25-basis-point increase in December, according to CME's FedWatch tool.

On Wednesday, minutes from the Federal Open Market Committee's October meeting could help illuminate the central bank's approach to near-term monetary policy. (Reuters)

articles.title: Hydropower hit record lows in the US Southwest this summer
articles.excerpt: The US Southwest generated 28% less electricity via hydropower between April and August than the 10-year average, according to new…
articles.fullText:
The US Southwest generated 28% less electricity via hydropower between April and August than the 10-year average, according to new data from the US Energy Information Administration.

Most hydropower plants in the US rely on dams to hold back water, creating reservoirs. The water can be released through turbines, generating electricity on demand. But an extreme, prolonged drought in the Colorado River Basin has resulted in dangerously low water levels in the Southwest’s two largest reservoirs, affecting the availability of this power source.

Residents and farmers in the US Southwest, a region that includes Arizona, New Mexico, and parts of Nevada and California, rely on water that melts in the spring from snowpack in the mountains and is slowly allowed to flow south via dam releases. Snowfall in the Rocky Mountains provides about 85% of the annual flow of the Colorado River . And in recent years, the river has seen record-low flows.

Two reservoirs along the Colorado River, Lake Powell and Lake Mead, have struggled to stay above the minimum level required for hydropower plants. At the end of September, Lake Powell’s depth was 3,518 feet, less than 1% above the level required to run the water through turbines that produce electricity at the Glen Canyon power plant. The Hoover Dam power plant requires 950 feet in Lake Mead, and that reservoir was 9% above the minimum in September.

Together, the two plants produced nearly seven terawatt-hours of electricity in 2025, enough to serve over 2 million people.

Low water levels have been an ongoing struggle for the region, which has been in a drought for 27 years. Meanwhile, climate change is continuing to shift rainfall and snowfall patterns across the region and around the world.

The effects of climate change on hydropower aren’t entirely straightforward globally—some regions will see more rain and snow because of shifting weather patterns, while others are likely to see less.

But it’s playing a role for hydropower availability, according to one 2022 review study . Rising temperatures bring more droughts, warmer winters means less snow and ice to fill the reservoirs, and more variability in precipitation can lead to alternating floods and droughts, making the power source less reliable.

Hydropower production is likely to be at its lowest level in over a decade in 2026 and tick even lower in 2027, according to projections from the EIA.

El Niño could provide some temporary relief. Sometimes this weather pattern can mean cooler, wetter conditions for the southern US. Heavy rains brought floods to the region in October and early November, and the water levels in Lake Powell rose more than 20 feet from their mid-September low. But the water is still quite low, and it’ll take much more to help reservoirs recover from decades of drought conditions.

Even as a changing climate complicates the availability of hydropower, the decline in capacity could push greenhouse-gas emissions higher. In 2023, energy-related greenhouse-gas emissions rose by 1.1% globally. A worldwide shortfall in hydropower generation accounted for about 40% of that rise, according to a report from the International Energy Agency.

articles.title: Working Holiday Scheme signed
articles.excerpt: Hong Kong and Chile today signed an agreement to establish a bilateral Working Holiday Scheme (WHS) for their youth. Secretary…
articles.fullText:
Hong Kong and Chile today signed an agreement to establish a bilateral Working Holiday Scheme (WHS) for their youth.

Secretary for Labour & Welfare Chris Sun and Minister of Foreign Affairs of Chile Francisco Pérez Mackenna signed the agreement on the sidelines of the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation Economic Leaders’ Meeting in Shenzhen. Chief Executive John Lee and President of Chile José Antonio Kast witnessed the signing.

Welcoming the agreement, Mr Sun said: “Chile is Hong Kong’s first WHS partner in Latin America. The scheme will provide young people from Hong Kong and Chile with opportunities to broaden their horizons and gain first-hand experience of living and working in a different cultural environment.”

Mr Pérez Mackenna said: “We are pleased to provide young people from Chile and Hong Kong with new opportunities to experience life in each other’s communities. Hong Kong’s unique blend of Eastern and Western cultures, international outlook and dynamic economy will offer Chilean youth an enriching experience. We also look forward to welcoming young people from Hong Kong to discover Chile’s rich culture, warm hospitality and natural beauty, thereby strengthening mutual understanding and people-to-people ties.”

Under the agreement, successful applicants can stay for up to 12 months in either Hong Kong or Chile. Participants may take up employment to finance their stay or enrol in short-term courses, subject to an annual quota of 100 places for each side.

This marks the 15th Working Holiday Scheme Hong Kong has established since 2001. Similar arrangements are already in place with New Zealand, Australia, Ireland, Germany, Japan, Canada, Korea, France, the United Kingdom, Austria, Hungary, Sweden, the Netherlands and Italy.

Over 109,000 Hong Kong youths have benefited from these schemes to date. Details on visa application procedures will soon be available on the websites of the Immigration Department and Chile’s National Migration Service .

articles.title: Stepping up maritime hub push
articles.excerpt: Secretary for Transport & Logistics Mable Chan has outlined how Hong Kong is upgrading and transforming its shipping industry to…
articles.fullText:
Secretary for Transport & Logistics Mable Chan has outlined how Hong Kong is upgrading and transforming its shipping industry to build a global maritime hub, aligning the city’s First Five-Year Plan with the National 15th Five-Year Plan. Highlighting Hong Kong’s role as the strategic southern gateway linking the Mainland with the world, she noted that the city serves as a "super-connector" and "super value-adder".

To consolidate and enhance Hong Kong’s status as an international shipping centre, the Government is adopting a dual-core strategy that boosts port competitiveness while fostering a vibrant, high-value maritime services cluster. Ms Chan expected that these efforts will strengthen the city’s resilience and attract fresh business opportunities for the sector.

"They can finance, they can build and also lead from Hong Kong as the base, to enter into a more rigorous and more complete holistic development of maritime and shipping development for Hong Kong," she said.

One of the key measures to enhance port competitiveness is the green transformation of the maritime industry. Hong Kong is the seventh-largest bunkering hub globally by volume, having completed over 210 green maritime fuel bunkering operations totalling more than 370,000 tonnes from January 2025 through the third quarter of 2026.

Ms Chan noted that Hong Kong holds strong potential to become a leading Green Maritime Fuel Bunkering & Trade Centre. To advance this goal, the Government has signed a Memorandum of Understanding with Zhanjiang in Guangdong to jointly establish Hong Kong’s very first Green Energy Corridor.

Ms Chan added that the Government will collaborate with relevant parties to develop national and international standards and certification systems for green shipping fuel. It will also leverage Hong Kong’s mature capital-raising platform to finance investments in green fuel shipping.

articles.title: APEC CEO Summit opens
articles.excerpt: Chief Executive John Lee attended the opening ceremony of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) CEO Summit in Shenzhen today and…
articles.fullText:
Chief Executive John Lee attended the opening ceremony of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) CEO Summit in Shenzhen today and met leaders of other economies during the day.

President Xi Jinping delivered a keynote speech at the opening ceremony, pointing out that APEC was born amid the waves of economic globalisation and enabled the Asia-Pacific to steer the course of the times. Noting that this year marks the third time China has hosted APEC, he said that China is ready to work with all parties to forge ahead with resolve, jointly build an Asia-Pacific community and bring prosperity for all in the region.

President Xi put forward four proposals: to uphold peace and stability, to build bridges of opening up and co-operation, to boost innovation to drive growth and to expand ways for mutual benefits and win-win outcomes. He also said China supports establishing a World Association for Bay Areas Economic Cooperation to deepen exchanges among bay areas worldwide and explore new ways for stronger regional economic co-operation.

Mr Lee said he was deeply encouraged and inspired by President Xi's keynote speech, noting that from a strategic and long-term perspective, it charted the course for Asia-Pacific co-operation. He added that the speech underscored the need to firmly uphold the post-war international order, resolve differences through dialogue and negotiation and respond to challenges through solidarity and collaboration to lay a solid foundation for long-term regional peace and stability.

The Chief Executive highlighted that as an APEC member economy, Hong Kong has long served as an important hub for regional economic and trade co-operation and is one of the world's most competitive economies. He noted that Hong Kong has consistently supported free trade and multilateralism, actively leveraging the APEC platform to continuously deepen international exchanges and co-operation.

Afterwards, Mr Lee met Malaysia's Prime Minister Dato' Seri Anwar Ibrahim and noted that the official opening of the Hong Kong Economic & Trade Office in Kuala Lumpur is deepening ties and investment promotion with the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) and neighbouring Asian countries. Highlighting Hong Kong's development as an international hub for high-calibre talent and a Muslim-friendly destination, Mr Lee welcomed more Malaysian students and visitors to Hong Kong.

Mr Lee then met Vietnam's President To Lam, noting that the two places share a vision for promoting high-quality development. He encouraged Vietnamese enterprises to leverage Hong Kong's advantages in connecting the Mainland and the world, using the city as a springboard to tap into the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area and seize more opportunities together.

In the afternoon, Mr Lee met Brunei's Sultan Haji Hassanal Bolkiah. Mr Lee said that Hong Kong's world-class capital markets, professional services and aviation and logistics network can strongly support deeper co-operation, expressing hope that both sides will further strengthen collaboration and complement each other's strengths.

In addition, Mr Lee met Thailand's Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul, noting that Thailand is developing its innovation and technology industries while Hong Kong is advancing the integrated development of education, technology and talent. He expressed hope that the two places would strengthen connectivity and co-operation in innovation and technology, encouraging more Thai enterprises to establish a presence in Hong Kong to expand into international markets.

Mr Lee then met Chile's President José Antonio Kast and witnessed the signing of the Working Holiday Scheme agreement between Hong Kong and Chile. Mr Lee said Hong Kong will continue to leverage its roles as a "super-connector" and "super value-adder" to strengthen bilateral co-operation in different areas.

Mr Lee thanked the leaders of Malaysia, Vietnam, Brunei and Thailand for their continued support for Hong Kong's early accession to the Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership and the joint promotion of regional economic development. He added that amid a complex and ever-changing international landscape, Hong Kong is actively expanding into diversified markets and deepening collaboration with ASEAN, Latin America and other countries of the Global South.

In the evening, Mr Lee was due to attend a welcome banquet for leaders and representatives of the participating economies. Tomorrow, he will attend the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting and hold bilateral talks with other regional leaders.

The Department of Justice (DOJ) of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region Government today signed a Memorandum of Co-operation (MOC) with Vietnam's Ministry of Foreign Affairs to strengthen co-operation on building capacity for the prevention and settlement of international disputes.

Signed by Secretary for Justice Paul Lam and Vietnam's Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs Le Anh Tuan, the pact provides a framework for Hong Kong and Vietnam to collaborate on building the capacity of legal officers with respect to international disputes in the economic, commercial and investment fields.

It is expected that the two places will benefit greatly from their enhanced co-operation under the pact.

It added that it will continue to pursue co-operation or partnership arrangements with other jurisdictions and international organisations.

The Electrical & Mechanical Services Department today announced a ban on the supply of four compact fluorescent lamp models that failed to reach its energy efficiency and/or performance specifications.

Imported by Beauty Shadow Co Ltd, the four products are sold under the Sunshine brand with the following model numbers: S-24A 23W B22 2700K, S-24A 23W E27 2700K, S-16A 12W E14 6400K, S-16A 12W E27 6400K.

The department has removed the lamps from the record of listed models under the Energy Efficiency (Labelling of Products) Ordinance. Supplying such products is no longer allowed in Hong Kong, with immediate effect.

Notices have been served to the importer, which will publish newspaper notices announcing supply of the products has been terminated.

articles.title: Green fuel platform to be developed
articles.excerpt: The Transport & Logistics Bureau today announced the establishment of the “Task Group on the Development of the Green Maritime…
articles.fullText:
The Transport & Logistics Bureau today announced the establishment of the “Task Group on the Development of the Green Maritime Fuel Trading Platform”, a collaboration with industry to advance Hong Kong’s development as a globally oriented, diverse and open green maritime fuel trading centre.

The bureau said that as an international maritime, financial and trading centre, Hong Hong has the unique advantage of being backed by China and enjoying global connectivity, adding that its financial and legal systems are aligned with international practices.

It added: “Coupled with the upcoming implementation of the half-rate tax concession for physical trading of eligible commodities, which include green fuels, Hong Kong is well-positioned to establish a market-driven, globally oriented green fuel trading centre, providing a platform that brings together green fuel supplies from the Chinese Mainland and around the world and connects them with demand from the global maritime industry.”

Bringing together energy traders, green fuel producers, think tanks, and maritime and energy organisations, to advise on the platform’s development, the task group will explore the establishment of a green fuel price index, based on actual transaction data, to provide reliable pricing references for the industry.

It will also advise on building a complete industry chain to support green fuel trading, with a view to attracting more stakeholders from the Chinese Mainland and overseas to trade green fuels in Hong Kong.

Founding members of the task group include the Hydrogen Energy Industry Promotion Association, CIMC Enric Holdings Limited, Hong Kong and China Gas Company Limited, TGT Group Limited, the International Green Fuels Alliance, Our Hong Kong Foundation and AEX Holdings, Ltd.

To drive the establishment of the trading platform, the bureau signed Memoranda of Understanding with multiple partners during Hong Kong Maritime Week. These covered platform development, price index development, solicitation of platform users and industry research.

articles.title: Mexican leader asks China for panda
articles.excerpt: Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum said on Tuesday that she asked President Xi Jinping for a panda for her country during…
articles.fullText:
Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum said on Tuesday that she asked President Xi Jinping for a panda for her country during a meeting in China.

"Next year marks the 55th anniversary of Mexico-China relations, and it's a very important milestone," Sheinbaum told reporters in Shenzhen.

"We discussed moving forward on tourism, and we also asked for a panda for the Chapultepec Zoo as part of this partnership," she said on the sidelines of the Apec summit.

"So it was a very good meeting – a very cordial and very frank one."

Chapultepec Zoo in Mexico City is home to the only known giant panda not owned by China, a 36-year-old female called Xin Xin.

It is the last in a line of giant pandas brought to Mexico in 1975.

Since the 1980s, China has operated a different policy in which it lends pandas for set periods and in return for a payment towards wild panda conservation efforts.

Sheinbaum also told Xi that relations with China are entering a "new era", while Xi called for ties to be elevated to a "a higher level" in light of a "complex" global situation.

Xi met various regional leaders on the Apec sidelines on Tuesday, among them Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney, Chilean President Jose Antonio Kast and Peruvian President Keiko Fujimori. (AFP)

Edited by Edmond Fong

articles.title: 'Unprecedented' Ukraine attack damages Crimean bridge
articles.excerpt: Ukrainian drones and missiles struck a vital bridge linking Russia to the occupied Crimean Peninsula, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said…
articles.fullText:
Ukrainian drones and missiles struck a vital bridge linking Russia to the occupied Crimean Peninsula, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said on Tuesday, calling it an “unprecedented” operation as Russia reported that its forces downed a record number of Ukrainian drones for the second straight day.

Zelenskyy portrayed the operation on the Kerch Bridge as a masterstroke, as Ukrainian forces gradually wore down Russian air defences for weeks before bombarding the prized target with a barrage of missiles and drones overnight.

Zelenskyy didn’t detail the damage, but the Ukrainian General Staff said that an arch and a span of the bridge’s road section collapsed, severing the road link, while the railway line was still standing but its arch was damaged.

Russia’s Investigative Committee said that the bridge was attacked by drones and sustained damage but didn’t elaborate.

The Kerch Bridge is a crucial link in moving military and civilian supplies from Russia to Crimea and to support troops on the front line.

The construction of the bridge, a potent symbol of Russia’s annexation of the peninsula in 2014, was inflammatory to Ukrainians.

“The symbol of the occupation has cracked,” the Ukrainian General Staff said in a statement.

Moscow’s forces, meanwhile, fired ballistic missiles and drones at Kyiv, hitting two of the Ukrainian capital’s main bridges and killing at least two people.

A recent escalation in aerial attacks came as Russia and Ukraine await a date for the next round of US-mediated talks aimed at ending the war.

US President Donald Trump said he plans to talk about the war in Ukraine during his highly anticipated meeting with President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin in China this week.

The Kerch Bridge attack was the culmination of weeks of preparatory strikes over seven stages of the operation, Zelenskyy said on social media.

Ukrainian forces knocked out defence systems, radars, electronic warfare equipment and other designated targets before launching Monday night's final attack, he said.

Domestically developed long-range drones struck the bridge's road section during the night while Ukraine's Neptune missiles and other drones aimed at the rail section, he said.

Flamingo precision-guided missiles delivered the final blow, he said.

The Russian-installed governor of Crimea, Sergei Aksyonov, said that traffic across the bridge was halted but rail traffic was restored by Tuesday afternoon.

He didn’t mention any damage.

Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said that “there is no doubt that the bridge will be restored and will be even better than it was before”.

Zelenskyy noted that Russia has battered Ukrainian infrastructure, especially the power grid, every day.

There were significant power outages in three Ukrainian regions on Tuesday, he said.

“We have repeatedly offered Russia steps toward de-escalation – and every proposal has been met with loud rejection,” he said.

Russian air defences downed 1,441 drones during a second straight night of major Ukrainian attacks, Russia’s Defence Ministry said on Tuesday.

That was a day after Russia said that it downed 1,336 Ukrainian drones in the highest number of interceptions it had reported so far during the war. (AP)

Edited by Edmond Fong

articles.fullText:
This is today’s edition of The Download , our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what’s going on in the world of technology.

The open-source movement wants Jensen Huang back

A petition to reinstate Jensen Huang as Nvidia CEO has attracted more than 115,000 signatures, including Elon Musk, but comb through the names, and you’ll notice a significant number come from a particular slice of the tech world: open-source AI.

Huang had become a sort of ringleader for open source, but his credibility as an advocate is now under threat. Revelations about Nvidia chips in China and a new rule in the US could deal a blow to both the movement’s reputation and its technical progress

Read the full story to find out why .

—James O’Donnell

This story is from The Algorithm, our weekly AI newsletter. Sign up to receive it in your inbox every Monday.

Roundtables: inside the quest for cognitive immortality

The quest to overcome the human brain’s limits is moving beyond science fiction. From gradual brain replacement to uploading memories to the cloud, researchers and technologists are exploring radical ways to extend human cognition. Today, MIT Technology Review examines these ideas in a live Roundtables discussion.

Join science editor Mary Beth Griggs and senior editor for biomedicine Antonio Regalado to explore what cognitive immortality could look like, and how close we might be to achieving it.

Tune in live today, Tuesday, November 17, at 5:00 p.m. GMT / 12:00 p.m. EST / 9:00 a.m. PST .

Want to join the conversation? Subscribe to MIT Technology Review for exclusive access to all our Roundtables.

The must-reads

I’ve combed the internet to find you today’s most fun/important/scary/fascinating stories about technology.

1 The US is tightening controls on China’s remote access to AI chips
It’s closed a loophole that let Chinese firms access US chips abroad. ( AP )
+  Xi may retaliate ahead of this week’s summit with Trump. ( Bloomberg $)
+ Nvidia is warning customers against renting chips to China. ( CNBC )
+ China is expanding AI distillation to work around curbs. ( Reuters $)
+ Nvidia privately said it can track chips to China. ( MIT Technology Review )

2 US hyperscale data centers are emitting as much CO2 as Denmark
A new study found emissions tripled between 2018 and 2025. ( Verge )
+ 400 data centers use more electricity than Michigan. ( Wired $)
+ Nations want to harness AI to cut emissions. ( Nature )
+ But AI models can quickly become climate crisis deniers. ( Guardian )

3 California has sued OpenAI over rogue AI hacking incidents
The attorney general said the company failed to protect the public. ( FT $)
+ And that it admitted to 80 cases of losing control of models. ( CNBC )
+ Who’s liable when AI agents go rogue? ( MIT Technology Review )

4 The Supreme Court has rejected Trump’s bid to cut research grants
Lower courts found the moves likely violated free speech rights. ( CBS )
+ Trump has dealt heavy blows to US science. ( MIT Technology Review )

5 Widespread online outages have hit major US banks
Thousands of customers reported account access problems. ( Gizmodo )
+ A separate outage delayed United Airlines flights. ( Reuters $)

6 Alice Huang’s husband built a data-center empire in China
He won government backing as his wife pursued Nvidia chips. ( WSJ $)
+ MAGA is using the scandal to weaken Trump’s Big Tech ties. ( Axios )

7 China has sacked a scientist after a child died in a gene-editing trial
The girl died after receiving an experimental therapy in 2025. ( Nature )

8 America’s EV boom is happening without car buyers

9 New cosmic data has challenged our model of the universe
The findings suggest dark energy may be weakening. ( Quanta )

10 A Buddhist sect plans to build an AI guru for Silicon Valley
It wants to create a model based on a collective mind. ( New Yorker $)

Quote of the day

“Export controls 2.0 is here.”

—Neil Shah, vice president of research at Counterpoint Research, tells Reuters that Washington has opened a new front in its campaign to slow China’s AI ambitions.

One more thing

Welcome to Kenya’s Great Carbon Valley: a bold new gamble to fight climate change

Kenya’s Great Rift Valley is home to five geothermal power stations, which harness clouds of steam to generate about a quarter of the country’s electricity. But some of the energy escapes into the atmosphere, while even more remains underground for lack of demand. That’s what brought Octavia Carbon here.

Last year, the startup began harnessing some of that excess energy to remove CO2 from the air. The company says the method is efficient, affordable, and—crucially—scalable. But the project also faces fierce opposition.

Read the full story on the future of Kenya’s “Great Carbon Valley.”

—Diana Kruzman

articles.title: Airport closer to sustainable aviation fuel facility
articles.excerpt: The Airport Authority signed a memorandum of understanding on Tuesday with Hong Kong and China Gas Company (Towngas) and EcoCeres…
articles.fullText:
The Airport Authority signed a memorandum of understanding on Tuesday with Hong Kong and China Gas Company (Towngas) and EcoCeres to develop a sustainable aviation fuel blending facility in the city to support the aviation industry's transition towards a more sustainable future.

The signing was witnessed by Chief Executive John Lee during the Asian Logistics, Maritime and Aviation Conference.

Also present for the signing were Secretary for Transport and Logistics Mable Chan, Airport Authority chief executive Vivian Cheung and Towngas chairman Peter Lee.

The MoU was signed by Airport Authority chief operating officer Steven Yiu, Towngas executive director and chief investment officer Alan Chan and EcoCeres CEO Matti Lievonen.

Under the agreement, the three parties will continue discussions on the design, construction and operation of a blending facility in Tuen Mun, with implementation subject to terms to be agreed between them.

In Hong Kong's first five-year plan, the government aims to achieve a sustainable aviation fuel consumption target of between one and three percent for flights departing from the airport by 2030.

John Lee announced in his Policy Address this year that the government would take forward the construction of a blending facility to build an end-to-end sustainable aviation fuel value chain and reduce logistics costs to make prices for greener jet fuel products more competitive.

The government is also collaborating with mainland authorities on the establishment of a sustainable aviation fuel production base in Dongguan.

The airport's existing fuel infrastructure is already capable of receiving, storing and uplifting pre-blended sustainable aviation fuel by airlines, with one local airline having successfully uplifted the fuel.

The Greater Bay Area is a proven model of how complementary strengths can generate opportunities far greater than the sum of their parts, Chief Executive John Lee told the Apec CEO Summit in Shenzhen on Tuesday.

"Prosperity is not something we can each win separately. It is something we can only build together," he said, urging Asia-Pacific economies to explore partnerships that combine their innovation and market knowledge with the Greater Bay Area's manufacturing capacity, capital and consumer markets.

Lee said the turnout of over 2,000 business and government leaders, including some 115 Fortune Global 500 companies, at the summit sends a clear message that economies of the region need open and continuing cooperation more than ever.

He said the Greater Bay Area, home to more than 88 million people and generating a GDP exceeding US$2.1 trillion, would rank about 12th globally if it were a standalone economy.

Lee said that under "One Country, Two Systems", Hong Kong has an indispensable role to play, describing it as the natural "super-connector" and "super value-adder" between the Greater Bay Area and the rest of the Asia-Pacific.

He invited the Asia-Pacific community to use Hong Kong as a springboard and business centre from which to seize the region's opportunities.

"Hong Kong, China stands ready to connect people, capital, ideas and opportunities so that we may all prosper and win the future. And that future begins right here."

Lee also said the Greater Bay Area is committed to the smooth flow of people, goods, capital and data.

articles.title: HK urged to offer tax cut for small commodity traders
articles.excerpt: The vice president of Our Hong Kong Foundation, Kenny Shui, has called on authorities to introduce an entry-level tax concession…
articles.fullText:
The vice president of Our Hong Kong Foundation, Kenny Shui, has called on authorities to introduce an entry-level tax concession to attract small commodity traders in a bid to drive the development of maritime services in the city.

The trade in commodities is linked to the shipment of such goods, which is why related maritime services are vital to the sector.

Shui made the remarks as the think tank released a research report on Tuesday, suggesting the SAR should focus on higher value-added maritime and professional services.

Speaking at a press conference, Shui said the government's existing half-tax concession helped attract medium-sized traders with an annual turnover of no less than HK$700 million, but such a threshold has excluded smaller traders with high growth potential.

Shui proposed a two-tier tax mechanism aimed at assisting traders whose turnover has yet to reach the threshold.

Under the proposal, the half-tax concession would be extended to cover small traders with potential for five years.

If a trader's annual turnover still fails to reach the HK$700 million threshold in the five-year period, the concession would cease, he said.

"Our current challenge is that compared with other competitors like Singapore, we do not have a lot of commodity traders," Shui said.

"So that's why we want to use the tax to attract them. For medium-sized payers, the government has a plan to use the half-tax to attract those payers.

"But for the entry-level [traders], as we do not have a half-tax plan, we just have the normal 16.5 percent tax. So that's why we are asking whether we can also have a half-tax for those entry-level payers to attract them to come to Hong Kong."

The foundation also called for enhanced marine insurance, ship leasing and maritime arbitration services.

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Tech fears continue to chip away at regional markets
articles.excerpt: Tech firms dragged Asian stock markets down again Tuesday as the fallout from the Nvidia crisis continued to rattle trading…
articles.fullText:
Tech firms dragged Asian stock markets down again Tuesday as the fallout from the Nvidia crisis continued to rattle trading floors, with US moves to tighten restrictions on Chinese access to chips adding to uncertainty.

In Hong Kong, the benchmark Hang Seng Index ended 245 points, or one percent, lower at 23,508 on turnover of HK$198.05 billion.

The tech index fell 43 points, or 1.1 percent, to 3,758 while the China enterprises index was 77 points, or one percent, lower at 7,904.

On the mainland, the Shanghai Composite Index closed down 17 points, or 0.5 percent, at 3,584 on turnover of 690.5 billion yuan.

The Shenzhen Component Index fell 52 points, or 0.49 percent, to 10,638 on turnover of 767.18 billion yuan while the ChiNext Index lost 27 points, or 1.2 percent, to close at 2,292 on turnover of 365.83 billion yuan.

In Tokyo, the Nikkei ended down 801 points, or 1.34 percent, at 58,860, with AI- and chip-related falls of 5.08 percent by Kioxia Holdings, 4.39 percent by Advantest and 3.95 percent by SoftBank Group contributing to the benchmark's losses.

The broader Topix slid 61 points, or 1.57 percent, to 3,840.

In Seoul, the Kospi closed 132 points, or 2.59 percent, lower at 4,968, down in a fourth consecutive session of losses, with chipmaking index heavyweights Samsung Electronics falling 3.3 percent and SK Hynix losing 1.96 percent.

The selloff comes as investors brace for the release of earnings from Wall Street titan Nvidia, which comes days after its boss Jensen Huang resigned over revelations of extramarital affairs.

Also in focus is the initial public offering of Claude-creator Anthropic, which is being seen as a test of confidence in the AI trade, which has been whipsawed in recent months by concerns over companies' eye-watering AI investments and their profitability.

Markets have been battered since the crisis broke at Nvidia, which is at the centre of a build-out in artificial intelligence that has helped propel global markets to record highs and boosted economic growth around the world.

Nvidia's earnings will be closely watched after the US market closes later Tuesday, or 8am on Wednesday Hong Kong time, with investors looking for signs of whether the AI boom can withstand the widening scandal.

Matt Weller at Forex.com said: "Data centre demand and guidance will be central.

"Investors will look for evidence that hyperscalers and other customers are sustaining their spending on AI infrastructure, and whether fourth-quarter guidance points to further growth."

Donald Trump on Monday backed calls from some of Silicon Valley's most powerful voices pushing for the swift return of Huang, with the US president downplaying national security concerns over allegations of possible spy links.

Adding to the downbeat mood was news that the US Commerce Department moved on Monday to close a loophole that allowed Chinese companies to access Nvidia's powerful AI chips remotely.

A new rule will force data centre operators in Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Brazil to get a licence from the United States allowing them to ship high-end AI chips from Nvidia and other American firms to clients in those countries.

"The proposed rules are aimed at limiting the remote use or diversion of cutting-edge US chips and extend the regulatory overhang facing the semiconductor industry," said National Australia Bank's Rodrigo Catril.

"The news also raises questions about the outlook for global AI infrastructure investment, particularly in jurisdictions that have become important hubs for data centre development." (Agencies)

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Welding or smoking suspected in Shek Kwu Chau fire
articles.excerpt: The Fire Services Department on Tuesday said a fire at a waste-management facility on an artificial island off Shek Kwu…
articles.fullText:
The Fire Services Department on Tuesday said a fire at a waste-management facility on an artificial island off Shek Kwu Chau last month was suspected to be related to welding works or smoking.

In a reply to media enquiries, the department said it had completed its investigation into the fire, which broke out on October 26, involving the collection of evidence at the scene and the taking of statements from relevant parties.

Its findings indicated that the fire originated on the upper level within the third incineration module area of the incineration building, the department said.

The investigation ruled out electrical faults, arson and spontaneous combustion of chemical substances as the cause.

The department said it had completed its report, which was referred to the Environmental Protection Department for follow-up.

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Shenzhen firms go extra mile in Apec workarounds
articles.excerpt: Shenzhen companies have adopted flexible working arrangements during the ongoing Apec-linked meetings, with some staff taking annual leave, working from…
articles.fullText:
Shenzhen companies have adopted flexible working arrangements during the ongoing Apec-linked meetings, with some staff taking annual leave, working from home or travelling off-peak.

Their flexibility came to light in an ongoing 100-hour all-media live broadcast titled "Apec China Year", which is being aired by Shenzhen Media Group in conjunction with Beijing Radio and Television and Shanghai Media Group to capture the host city's preparations for the summit and supporting events.

Yao Peitong of Harbin Institute of Technology Pengze, Shenzhen, a robotics company, said it was only following government advice by having only four of its 15-strong workforce back in the office.

Meituan, for its part, has introduced 10 measures from Monday to Friday to ease pressure on delivery riders.

Yuan Min, a rider protection manager, said late deliveries across Shenzhen would not be penalised.

Meituan's Shenzhen head, Niu Dexu, said the company's app had, together with the authorities, also launched a Chinese-English food map to facilitate visitors seeking to sample the city's varied fare.

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: John Lee arrives in Shenzhen for Apec meeting
articles.excerpt: Chief Executive John Lee arrived in Shenzhen on Tuesday to attend the Apec Economic Leaders’ Meeting, beginning a trip aimed…
articles.fullText:
Chief Executive John Lee arrived in Shenzhen on Tuesday to attend the Apec Economic Leaders’ Meeting, beginning a trip aimed at promoting Hong Kong’s role in Apec's "China Year".

In a post on social media, Lee said he was “deeply delighted” to take part in the meeting as China hosts Apec for the third time.

On arrival, he was received by a representative of the First Bureau of the Hong Kong and Macao Work Office of the Communist Party of China Central Committee.

Lee pointed to last month’s Apec Finance Ministers’ Meeting — held in Hong Kong for the first time — as evidence of the city’s unique advantage under "One Country, Two Systems": connecting the mainland and the world while contributing to financial cooperation within the regional body.

During the trip, Lee will also attend the Apec CEO Summit, including its discussion session and opening ceremony, to exchange views with political and business leaders from other economies.

He will hold bilateral meetings with leaders of other economies to explore mutually beneficial cooperation opportunities for Hong Kong.

Lee described Shenzhen and Hong Kong as sister cities and close partners within the Greater Bay Area, noting that the two places have advanced side by side in artificial intelligence, innovation and technology.

He expressed hope that Apec economies gathering in the “City of Miracles” would explore opportunities together, guided by openness, innovation and cooperation.

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Xi, Carney deepen strategic partnership in talks
articles.excerpt: President Xi Jinping on Tuesday said the improvement and development of China-Canada relations is a right choice that serves the…
articles.fullText:
President Xi Jinping on Tuesday said the improvement and development of China-Canada relations is a right choice that serves the interests of both peoples and is conducive to world peace, stability, development and prosperity.

In a meeting with Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney in Shenzhen on the sidelines of the Apec summit, he said the development of China-Canada relations over the years had shown that mutual respect, equality and mutual benefit, and seeking common ground while respecting differences are essential.

China, Xi said, stands ready to work with Canada to further advance the new type of strategic partnership between the two countries.

Exchanges and cooperation across various fields have fully resumed, Xi pointed out, since since the two leaders agreed, during Carney's visit to Beijing in January, to launch a strategic partnership.

Xi outlined, according to Xinhua, four proposals for advancing bilateral ties: fostering a more "accurate understanding" of each other's development paths; deepening cooperation in trade, energy, agriculture and finance while expanding into sectors such as the green, digital and e-commerce economies; strengthening people-to-people cultural exchanges; and upholding the multilateral trading system.

"Stronger communication and cooperation between China and Canada will benefit not only our two countries but also Asia-Pacific and the world," Xi told Carney.

Carney's office said China would be cutting tariffs on more Canadian exports including pork and seafood as the prime minister hailed "greater predictability and stability" in bilateral relations in his meeting with Xi.

Carney said Canada was well ahead of schedule in its goal of boosting exports to China "by 50 percent by the end of this decade".

A major plank of Carney's economic strategy is to reduce Canada's heavy reliance on the United States, which has imposed hefty tariffs on many Canadian products.

Xi and Carney agreed to extend and expand a preliminary arrangement to improve access to the Chinese market for Canada's farmers and seafood harvesters, a statement from Carney's office said.

China will provide additional tariff relief for around C$400 million in Canadian exports, including frozen pork cuts and fish and seafood.

In exchange, Canada has agreed to extend by two years existing remission measures for certain Chinese steel and aluminium products that are currently set to expire at the end of 2026, the statement said.

Tuesday's talks marked the third meeting between Carney and Xi since Carney became prime minister; the two also met on the sidelines of last year's Apec summit in South Korea.

Chinese automakers BYD, Geely and Chery have taken steps to enter the Canadian market since Ottawa approved annual imports of 49,000 cars at a tariff rate of 6.1 percent.

The quota is set to rise to 70,000 cars over five years.
