China also lowered tariffs on Canadian canola seed following Carney's January visit, and recently extended tariff relief for Canadian canola meal, lobsters, crabs and peas for two more years.

Shipments of Canadian crude oil to China have risen about 37 percent in 2026, according to a calculation based on LSEG data. (Agencies)

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Ovaries wrongly removed in private hospital op
articles.excerpt: Local authorities on Tuesday made public two incidents in September, one of which saw both ovaries of a 45-year-old woman…
articles.fullText:
Local authorities on Tuesday made public two incidents in September, one of which saw both ovaries of a 45-year-old woman mistakenly removed during surgery, the Department of Health said.

The department said, in reply to enquiries on Tuesday, that the woman had undergone a laparoscopic hysterectomy and bilateral salpingectomy.

During the procedure, which was performed at CUHK Medical Centre, both ovaries were wrongly removed.

The woman is in stable condition.

Department officials said there was no evidence to show that the private hospital had breached applicable requirements under the code of practice in terms of premises, manpower or equipment that led to the incident.

CUHK Medical Centre said it was highly concerned about the case.

It said it apologised to the patient and her family, explained the incident to authorities and provided appropriate medical follow-up and support.

The medical centre added it had conducted a comprehensive review and would implement appropriate follow-up and improvement measures in light of the findings.

The second case involved a 27-year-old woman at a day procedure centre who was mistaken for another patient and was given dental scaling treatment.

The woman is also in a stable condition.

The department said it had followed up on the two cases immediately after being notified and requested that the facilities concerned submit investigation reports within four weeks.

It said it had received the reports and completed its investigations.

The facilities concerned have taken improvement measures and the department would continue to monitor their implementation.

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Apple faces court crunch over iPhone obsolescence
articles.excerpt: Apple is to stand trial in Paris in June on suspicion of having organised the planned obsolescence of various iPhone…
articles.fullText:
Apple is to stand trial in Paris in June on suspicion of having organised the planned obsolescence of various iPhone models by preventing repairs outside official outlets, a source said on Tuesday.

The case brought by French prosecutors against the US tech giant on charges of "obstructing repair and refurbishment" is a first, campaign group Stop Planned Obsolescence said, welcoming the move after filing a complaint on December 7, 2022.

"We strongly contest these unfounded allegations," Apple said.

Planned obsolescence refers to techniques used by manufacturers to deliberately shorten the lifespan of their products, generally electronic devices, thereby encouraging consumers to discard and replace them more frequently.

According to the source, Apple Distribution International and parent company Apple Inc are due to appear in court for a four-day trial starting on June 17.

They are accused of preventing repairs to a range of iPhone models for more than two and a half years, from November 2021 to July 2024.

Apple is accused of configuring its smartphone software to "make it impossible to repair or refurbish" devices outside its authorised network, the source added.

The alleged aim was to boost sales of Apple's flagship product and increase the revenue of the multinational, which now generates more than US$400 billion a year, about half of that from iPhone sales. (AFP)

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Tech leaders say EV innovation, robotaxis key for Apec
articles.excerpt: The founder of the world's largest electric vehicle battery maker on Tuesday said opportunities in the Asia-Pacific region outweigh challenges…
articles.fullText:
The founder of the world's largest electric vehicle battery maker on Tuesday said opportunities in the Asia-Pacific region outweigh challenges and that innovation is the key to unlocking them.

Speaking at the Apec CEO Summit in Shenzhen, Robin Zeng of Contemporary Amperex Technology Limited (CATL) said a company's first goal is to make money, but that its purpose as it grows should be to benefit people.

He said this is what motivates him to persist, adding that CATL is focused on innovation and on sharing the benefits of advances made across the region.

"We really focus on innovations," Zeng said.

"So if you have technology innovation, product innovation, solution innovation, then they can come up with a solution to share in this region.

"For example, everyone now is focused on the EV.

"We are more focused on the infrastructure of the EV, so battery swapping is one of the innovations, which can help all the EV cars swap the batteries in 99 seconds. So it's very fast.

"This can already be applied to this region. This is we're talking about a business model innovation."

Speaking at the same panel discussion, Baidu chief executive Robin Li highlighted driverless ride-hailing vehicles as a prime example of artificial intelligence's real-world potential.

"It's a real application, and people can really benefit from that," he said.

"It benefits people's daily lives. Every year, more than a million people get killed on the roads.

"But when robotaxi is operating, its safety record is about 10 times better than that of a human driver."

Li said that with China and the United States gradually opening the way for for autonomous vehicles, he hoped other places in Asia would follow suit.

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Apec CEO Summit attendance over 2,000, says chair
articles.excerpt: More than 2,000 chief executives and representatives will attend the Apec CEO Summit in Shenzhen on Tuesday and Wednesday, summit…
articles.fullText:
More than 2,000 chief executives and representatives will attend the Apec CEO Summit in Shenzhen on Tuesday and Wednesday, summit chairman Ren Hongbin said.

He said discussions on the first day of the event would cover seven topics, among which are artificial intelligence, sustainable development, digital economy and development opportunities for the Greater Bay Area and the Asia-Pacific region.

“For a long time, the business community has actively supported, participated in and promoted the cooperation and development in the Asia-Pacific region,” Ren said.

“By pushing major development, prosperity and connectivity in the region, it has made Asia-Pacific the most dynamic region in the global economy and a primary engine for growth.”

Ren, also chairman of the China Council for the Promotion of International Trade, said President Xi Jinping would attend the summit’s opening ceremony on Wednesday and deliver a speech.

Another 11 leaders of Apec economies would also attend the summit, he added.

Ren expressed hope that summit participants could achieve consensus and cooperation during discussions.

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Apec talks under way on outcome document: official
articles.excerpt: Consultations on the outcome document for the upcoming Apec Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen have already begun, with parties anchoring…
articles.fullText:
Consultations on the outcome document for the upcoming Apec Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen have already begun, with parties anchoring on the core goal of building an Asia-Pacific community, according to Chen Xu, chair of the 2026 Apec Senior Officials' Meeting.

Speaking at the Apec Leaders' Meeting Week media centre in Shenzhen, he said the work aims to build on the many practical cooperation outcomes already achieved and further forge consensus.

Chen said the main focus is to push for the release of an ambitious leaders' outcome document that sets out the shared vision and actions for building an Asia-Pacific community, and to actively promote practical outcomes in trade connectivity and innovation, injecting new momentum into Apec cooperation in these areas.

He said he believes the leaders' meeting will be a complete success with the joint efforts of all parties.

Chen noted that China is hosting Apec for the third time.

Over the past year, he said, preparations have been carried out around the theme of building an Asia-Pacific community and promoting common prosperity, as well as the three priority areas of openness, innovation and cooperation.

More than 300 meetings and events have, he pointed out, so far been held in 16 cities across the country, with representatives from various economies holding extensive and in-depth discussions and reaching a rich consensus on issues of common concern and areas of cooperation.

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Silence is golden for Shenzheners and Apec visitors
articles.excerpt: Shenzhen has embraced an unusual quiet as it prepares to host world leaders this week, with car horns banned, delivery…
articles.fullText:
Shenzhen has embraced an unusual quiet as it prepares to host world leaders this week, with car horns banned, delivery drones grounded and residents urged to leave vehicles at home.

The meeting of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum, in which presidents Donald Trump of the United States and Vladimir Putin of Russia will attend, is a chance for Shenzhen to show off its transformation from an agricultural backwater into the high-tech – and orderly, officials hope to show – city it is today.

More than 1.5 million local car owners have pledged to stay off the roads in exchange for Apec car stickers and, if they keep their word, transit cards worth up to 100 yuan.

From Tuesday, cars with out-of-town plates will be barred from most city districts during the day, Shenzhen traffic police said.

Even the city's ubiquitous e-bike riders have been asked to dismount in return for discounts on insurance, while parked bikes are being removed from main streets.

Many downtown areas have been spruced up for the summit.

The venue stands beside Honey Lake, or Xiangmihu, which was home to one of Asia's largest amusement parks when it opened in 1985.

The park's long-disused roller coaster was torn down in 2024 to make way for a financial district.

Today the lakeside area is lined with fresh flower beds and newly paved roads.

Shenzhen has encouraged employers to allow remote work, staggered hours or paid leave.

Some residents are making the most of it.

John, a middle-school teacher, is heading to the southwestern city of Chongqing.

"I just want to relax and enjoy cheap food, and come back when things are back to normal," he said.

On the roads, the hush owes much to a citywide ban on beeping that came in this month, enforced by acoustic cameras and fines starting at 300 yuan.

Shenzhen has long restricted horn use, but the new rules have been widely publicised.

"People are cutting in much more dangerously, you've just got to sit and watch," said Liu, a 29-year-old working in media, on the ban on using her car horn.

Drones, one of the city's most famous exports, have been grounded, with Meituan suspending drone deliveries for 10 days.

Preparations extend to wardrobes.

An office worker called Lin said her employer had told staff not to wear clothing printed with English phrases they did not understand, in case they were inadvertently displaying obscenities.

Still, across the city, tens of thousands of people are wearing red jackets with "volunteer" written on them, including security guards at housing compounds. (Reuters)

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: HK to become centre for maritime business: CE
articles.excerpt: Hong Kong will move beyond being a port through which goods pass and become a centre where maritime business of…
articles.fullText:
Hong Kong will move beyond being a port through which goods pass and become a centre where maritime business of every kind is conducted, Chief Executive John Lee said on Tuesday.

"More than a port, through which goods move, Hong Kong will become a centre where maritime business of every kind is conducted," Lee said at the opening of the 16th Asian Logistics, Maritime and Aviation Conference.

"In aviation we are capitalising on the three runway system to expand our flight network and enhance capacity. We're committed to giving businesses greater reach and more choices in moving goods through Hong Kong," he said.

He said the city is also pursuing cargo growth and high-value maritime services, from ship finance and insurance to management and legal services.

"Growth opens markets. Innovation gives businesses the tools to compete. Sustainability prepares them for the future," he said.

Lee said the city's expanding partner port network supports its ambitions.

Partnerships were established last year with Guangxi Port, Dalian Port and Chile's Centennial Port, and new ties are being forged this year with ports in Shanghai, Piraeus in Greece, Yangpu in Hainan and Qingdao in Shandong, he said.

He revealed that Hong Kong would sign a memorandum of understanding with the Ministry of Transport's Global Sustainable Transport Innovation and Knowledge Centre to promote the country's sustainable transportation certification system internationally.

"We are also working with our Greater Bay Area partners to advance cargo movements and develop high value logistics services, and in doing so we will make Hong Kong a more competitive gateway connecting Chinese mainland production with international markets," he said.

In aviation, Lee said an MOU would be signed between the Airport Authority, Towngas and a Hong Kong-based company for a dedicated sustainable aviation fuel blending facility.

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: HK, region track Wall St retreat amid tech jitters
articles.excerpt: Asian shares followed Wall Street lower on Tuesday, weighed down by weakness in technology companies after the United States stepped…
articles.fullText:
Asian shares followed Wall Street lower on Tuesday, weighed down by weakness in technology companies after the United States stepped up efforts to curb China's access to advanced AI chips, escalating the race for technological dominance.

In Hong Kong, the benchmark Hang Seng Index opened down 232 points, or 0.98 percent, at 23,521.

The China enterprises index was 70 points, or 0.88 percent, lower at 7,911 while the tech index fell 41 points, or 1.09 percent, to 3,760.

Up north, the Shanghai Composite Index slipped 16 points, or 0.47 percent, to open at 3,585.

The Shenzhen Component Index was 85 points, or 0.8 percent, down at 10,605 while the ChiNext Index fell 20 points, or 0.86 percent, to 2,299.

In Tokyo, the Nikkei opened down 366 points, or 0.61 percent, at 59,295 and its losses widened to put the 225-strong benchmark 792 points lower at one stage before lunch as investors remained on the sidelines ahead of Nvidia's third-quarter earnings and Anthropic's initial public offering.

In Seoul, the Kospi opened 92 points, or 1.81 percent, lower at 5,008 before regaining some ground to be 71 points down at one stage before noon as chipmaker Samsung Electronics fell 2.41 percent while peer SK Hynix lost 0.63 percent.

The opening losses came as Washington said overnight it would further restrict China's access to advanced AI chips from companies like Nvidia.

The new rule restricts shipments of advanced chips to data centres like those in Thailand and Malaysia that Chinese companies have used to access computing power to train AI models.

"This is a meaningful escalation because it extends restrictions from physically buying advanced chips to accessing their computing power remotely," said Charu Chanana, chief investment strategist at Saxo.

"The impact could be significant for providers heavily reliant on Chinese customers training advanced AI models. They could face lower utilisation, weaker pricing and delays to expansion, while licensing uncertainty could make financing new projects harder."

A key moment for markets on Tuesday will be Nvidia's earnings after the bell, with investors watching for signs of whether its debt-fuelled AI spending will continue into 2027 and how Jensen Huang's departure as CEO could affect the company's influence across the AI ecosystem.

Still, senior figures within the US tech industry, including SpaceX tycoon Elon Musk, as well as US President Donald Trump have thrown their support behind Huang, with Trump signalling on Monday that he would welcome the Nvidia founder being reinstated as CEO of the company.

"Jensen obviously has two things going: he has a family situation which is a rough deal, and what he wants to do is to sell chips," Trump said.

"We prohibited him from selling the important chips, the modern day chips. But frankly, selling the other chips is a good thing, not a bad thing." (Agencies)

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: JPMorgan bug causes transaction problems at US banks
articles.excerpt: Thousands of customers reported difficulty accessing online accounts at several major US banks and the money transfer service Zelle on…
articles.fullText:
Thousands of customers reported difficulty accessing online accounts at several major US banks and the money transfer service Zelle on Monday after a technical issue at JPMorgan Chase caused ripple effects throughout the financial system.

However, Chase said that the technical problems were not the result of a cyberattack, and that it was working to bring banking services back online by the end of the day on Monday.

“JPMorgan Chase has experienced a temporary issue related to a software bug in an on-premise hardware system – it is not cyber-related,” said Joe Evangelisti, spokesman for the bank.

The disruption comes days after two major outages affected other parts of the US economy: A major outage by Microsoft happened Thursday and lasted for hours, severely impacting services including Outlook, Teams and AI assistant Copilot. An outage affecting the nation’s air traffic control system Friday grounded all US flights for several hours and continued to disrupt air travel across the country over the weekend.

In the same statement, Evangelisti said that this was a Chase-only issue.

“This is not a systemic issue – other banks may have been impacted by slowness in transactions only to the extent that they were a party to a transaction with us,” he said.

Monday's technical issues seemed to be centred at Chase customers and customers at other banks trying to transact with Chase. Those banks, including Bank of America and Citigroup, were not having issues with their banking services.

A spokesman for US Bank said its systems were not directly impacted but that “clients attempting to send or receive Zelle payments with another financial institution may experience transaction delays.”

Zelle is the peer-to-peer payment system that major US banks use to allow customers to send money to friends and family at near-instant speed. Zelle is owned by Arizona-based Early Warning Services, which in turn is owned by financial institutions including Bank of America, Capital One, JPMorgan Chase, PNC Bank, Truist, US Bank and Wells Fargo.

A spokesman for Early Warning Services said the Zelle network was fully operational.

“An issue at the financial institutions may be delaying Zelle payments for some of their customers,” the spokesman said.

Some Chase customers received a message that said, “Some services aren't available. We’re working on them. Please try back later.” (AP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: Alcaraz sweeps aside Tiafoe in ATP Finals opener
articles.excerpt: Carlos Alcaraz looked in ominous form on Monday as he began his bid to win the ATP Finals for the…
articles.fullText:
Carlos Alcaraz looked in ominous form on Monday as he began his bid to win the ATP Finals for the first time by cruising past Frances Tiafoe in straight sets, 6-2, 6-2.

World number three Alcaraz took just over an hour to deal with American Tiafoe and show why he is the favourite to win the whole thing in Turin, where he was the beaten finalist last year.

Since returning in August from a wrist injury that kept him off the tour for four months, Alcaraz has won three of the five tournaments he has entered, most recently the Paris Masters.

Alcaraz, 25, can book his place in the semi-finals on Wednesday by beating Italian Flavio Cobolli, who in the absence of former world number one Jannik Sinner is the crowd favourite.

"Sometimes I feel really comfortable," Alcaraz said.

"I feel like I'm better than the opponent in every aspect of the game.

"If I qualify to the semi-final or not, I think it's a great experience, a great week, getting experience," he added.

Tiafoe had a nightmare debut match at the season-ending tournament, the 28-year-old having no answer to Alcaraz's speed and power.

Only briefly in the second set did he look like challenging his opponent, a seven-time Grand Slam winner, when at 3-2 down he wasted three opportunities to break back. (AFP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: Palace appoint Thomas Frank as manager
articles.excerpt: Crystal Palace appointed Thomas Frank as their new manager on Monday, handing the Dane the daunting task of lifting the…
articles.fullText:
Crystal Palace appointed Thomas Frank as their new manager on Monday, handing the Dane the daunting task of lifting the struggling club off the bottom of the Premier League table.

The former Brentford and Tottenham boss succeeds Pierre Sage, who was sacked last week after 16 games in charge.

The Frenchman was unable to build on the legacy of his predecessor Oliver Glasner, who oversaw the most successful period in the club's history.

Glasner led the south London club to their first-ever major trophy, beating Manchester City to win the FA Cup in 2025, and won the Uefa Conference League last season.

"It's an honour to sit here and be in charge of this fantastic football club. I'm really, really looking forward to it," Frank said in a Palace statement.

"Crystal Palace is an iconic club in England and in the Premier League. I will do everything I possibly can to help and support the players and everyone around the place and I'm really looking forward to meeting them."

Frank, who has signed a two-and-a-half-year deal, enjoyed great success during seven years at Brentford, leading the Bees into the top flight for the first time in 74 years in 2021 and establishing the club in the Premier League.

His work in west London earned the 53-year-old a move to Tottenham in June 2025 but he lasted just eight months as Spurs struggled.

Palace hope Frank can rekindle the highs of his time at Brentford with similar resources at Selhurst Park.

"I'm delighted to be able to welcome Thomas to Crystal Palace," said Palace chairman Steve Parish. "He has a proven track record of both creating winning teams and improving players, making him the perfect fit for our club."

Sage paid the price after four straight league defeats left Palace at the bottom of the table.

He was hindered by the departures of Maxence Lacroix to Chelsea and Daniel Munoz, who reunited with Glasner at Nottingham Forest.

Palace have the worst defensive record in the Premier League, shipping 24 goals in 10 matches.

They will be hoping for an instant improvement as they prepare to face relegation rivals Coventry and Hull in their next two league games.

They also sit 21st in the 36-team Europa League table with four games of the league phase remaining. (AFP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: Germany run riot over Netherlands in Nations League
articles.excerpt: Florian Wirtz scored twice and Brajan Gruda contributed a goal and two assists as Germany cruised to a 5-0 win…
articles.fullText:
Florian Wirtz scored twice and Brajan Gruda contributed a goal and two assists as Germany cruised to a 5-0 win over the Netherlands in Berlin to reach the Nations League quarter-finals on Monday.

Derry Scherhant and Nico Schlotterbeck also got on the scoresheet as the Germans cut the visitors to shreds in the most impressive match of Jurgen Klopp's six-game stint as coach.

It was Germany's biggest win over their neighbours since a 7-0 victory in 1959.

"The game was outstanding," Klopp told German broadcaster ARD. "We scored unbelievable goals. It was just insane. A fantastic football match and a magnificent experience. I wouldn't have even dared to wish for all of this."

Klopp singled out Gruda and Scherhant, two players he has given their debuts, for special praise.

"Boy can those two play. But the amount of work they put in, it's immense. That's what defines a team, and plenty of others can play football too."

So often criticised for a lack of end product since his big-money move to Liverpool in 2025, Wirtz has scored in four in his past four games for Germany.

"We hope that we can make it fun for the fans. It was definitely fun for us, especially in the second-half," Wirtz told ARD.

The Dutch defeat was the first since their coach Xavi Hernandez took charge but, despite Greece's 1-0 win over Serbia on Monday, they also qualified for the final eight, although the last German goal dropped them to second in the group.

The Netherlands offered little in attack after Germany's second and missed injured captain Virgil van Dijk at the back, with the hosts cutting through a flimsy defence at will.

"I'm really sad, because before the game I was really proud," Xavi told reporters.

"Today it was not about the football, but about speed and about (our) values."

"I want to say sorry to our supporters, because today we showed our worst face. It's part of the process... We need to keep going and work on our values."

Germany knew only a victory would give them a realistic chance of reaching the quarters, with coach Klopp describing the match as a "final."

The game, a rematch of the 1974 World Cup final won by Germany in Munich, began with both sides risk averse and reluctant to move forward.

The Dutch had the first good chance when Jurrien Timber found Crysencio Summerville unmarked on the penalty spot, but the winger lost his footing before getting a shot away.

Just after the half hour, the Berlin-born-and-raised Scherhant latched onto a cross from Freiburg teammate Philipp Treu but hit the far post.

Nine minutes later, Scherhant had another chance from the same blade of grass and this time curled a lovely effort across the face of goal and inside the post.

"I don't think it could have gone any better, to score the opener here in my city. I don't think I could have dreamed of better. It's unbelievable," Scherhant said.

The Germans continued their assault on the Dutch penalty area after the break, Wirtz adding another with a solo effort on the hour. The Liverpool winger dribbled from left to right and back centrally before lifting a shot in off the left post from the penalty arc.

Schlotterbeck headed in from a Gruda free-kick with 65 minutes gone.

RB Leipzig winger Gruda laid on another goal six minutes later when he tore down the right and found Wirtz, who hammered in off the bottom of the crossbar.

In his first Germany match on home soil and just his second overall, Gruda then added one of his own, tapping in a Scherhant shot which rebounded off the post.

"We don't mind who we play. We want to play attacking football. We want to score goals and dominate the opponent. And I think we did that perfectly," said Wirtz.

"We want to keep going next year. We want to get better. I think we've taken some great steps in our development as a team." (AFP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: Uefa backs France's Diallo to stand against Infantino
articles.excerpt: European football's governing body Uefa has given its "unanimous" backing to French Football Federation chief Philippe Diallo to stand against…
articles.fullText:
European football's governing body Uefa has given its "unanimous" backing to French Football Federation chief Philippe Diallo to stand against incumbent Gianni Infantino in March's Fifa presidential election, it said in a statement on Monday.

The body said that Diallo had been "invited...to stand as a candidate in the Fifa presidential election in March 2027" and that European national associations had "unanimously pledged their full support."

The deadline for rival candidates to declare themselves is this Wednesday, November 18.

Uefa, which boasts 55 member associations, said Diallo "has accepted the invitation to stand" and that his candidature is set to be confirmed at a meeting of the French federation (FFF) on Tuesday.

Under its Slovenian president Aleksander Ceferin, Uefa has led the opposition to Infantino since his announcement in late July of a project to sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors.

Infantino quickly abandoned the proposal in the face of widespread uproar, but Uefa has since gone to a court in Florida in an attempt to gather evidence for a potential complaint of "criminal mismanagement" against the Fifa president in Switzerland.

Uefa had been struggling to find a credible candidate to stand against Infantino in the election, which will take place at the Fifa Congress on March 18 next year in the Moroccan capital, Rabat.

Concacaf chief Victor Montagliani had been mooted as a candidate, but the Canadian later announced his desire to stand for a new term as the head of his confederation, which covers North and Central America and the Caribbean.

The Asian Football Confederation, which consists of 47 member associations, announced last month that it was backing Infantino for re-election.

Diallo said in September that the FFF was withdrawing its backing for Infantino in the election.

"We believe that the trust placed in the Fifa president has been betrayed, and that the way in which the governance of world football is envisaged no longer reflects us," he said at the time.

Diallo, the 63-year-old son of a Senegalese boxing champion, has been president of the FFF since January 2023.

He was initially appointed to the post on an interim basis when previous chief Noel Le Graet was forced to stand down following a series of controversies.

Diallo, from Saint-Nazaire on France's Atlantic coast, was then elected to the role by a large majority in June of that year, before being re-elected in December 2024 for a new four-year term.

Infantino, a former Uefa secretary general, has been in charge of Fifa since 2016. (AFP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: United Airlines tech glitch delays hundreds of flights
articles.excerpt: United Airlines on Monday said that it had resolved a technology issue that delayed departing flights, just days after a…
articles.fullText:
United Airlines on Monday said that it had resolved a technology issue that delayed departing flights, just days after a malfunction in the Federal Aviation Administration’s network prompted a nationwide ground stop in the United States.

Chicago-based United said in a statement that while some flights were delayed because of the issue on Monday afternoon, flights that were in the air and flights on its United Express regional network were not affected. The airlines also said there was “no indication that this was a cybersecurity-related issue.”

United apologised to customers for the inconvenience on social media. It resolved the issue about 1.5 hours after pilots first began reporting problems to air traffic controllers.

United did not immediately provide details about which of the airlines systems were affected, but pilots told air traffic controllers that the problem was related to United’s system that helps them determine a plane's final weight to ensure it can safely take off.

A recording posted on the ATC app showed a United pilot in Houston asking the tower for permission to stay put at the gate until the system was working again. The app combines live air traffic control radio feeds with real-time visual aircraft tracking.

The flight tracking website FlightAware showed United with 418 delayed flights late Monday afternoon.

The United computer problem is just the latest high-profile technology meltdown in recent days.

Earlier on Monday, thousands of people reported being unable to access their online accounts at several major US banks after JPMorgan Chase had a technical problem.

On Friday, the FAA ordered every flight grounded because a new router that was installed malfunctioned and overwhelmed the ageing air traffic control system.

And one day earlier, Microsoft experienced a major disruption to its Outlook email service. Microsoft said on Saturday that services were fully restored. (AP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: Villagers in northern Laos are afraid to use river water after rare-earth pond spill
articles.excerpt: Government and Chinese-financed mining company say water is safe, but residents are skeptical after animal deaths.
articles.fullText:
Read a version of this story in Lao .
After ponds at a Chinese-financed rare-earth mining operation burst and potentially contaminated two rivers in northern Laos, villagers living downstream told Radio Free Asia they don’t think the water is safe.
Villagers in northern Laos fear using river water after drainage ponds at a Chinese-financed rare earth mine burst upstream from their communities.
On Nov. 1, several drainage ponds began to overflow at the Laos-China Rare Mineral Development Company North 2 Ltd. in Houaphanh province’s Xam Neua district. The water from the ponds drained into the Nam Vaen River, which flows into the Nam Xam River, which crosses the border into Vietnam.
There are approximately 18 affected villages that rely on the two rivers for agriculture, and this is the third rare-earth spill in the area after similar incidents in February 2024 and April 2026.
Authorities began an investigation on Nov. 4, consulting with officials from the mining company, who assured the government that the water was safe. But as early as Nov. 6, residents living downstream from the mining operation reported that fish were dying. Later, reports surfaced that birds and livestock like cows and pigs had also died. Authorities suspended mining indefinitely on Nov. 13.
A dead cow lies in the waters of the Nam Xam river in Houaphanh province, Laos, Nov. 13, 2026.
(Samakhom Khet 4) The local government should have visited the affected villages instead of just talking to the company, a resident of Muang Vaen village told RFA on condition of anonymity for security reasons.
“They say there is no contamination, telling the people to be confident that nothing is wrong, but right now, fish are dying in massive numbers,” the villager said. “They didn’t go inspect the downstream area where the incident happened – they didn’t come at all. They went to the site up at the top, listening to them, listening to the company at the project site saying ‘nothing is wrong, this and that.’ They’re just trying to keep people from panicking.”
During the investigation, the mining company told the government that the pond that burst was a natural water storage pond, not a chemical waste storage pond. The company stated it has repaired the water pipes and will compensate damages to two families whose rice fields were damaged, in accordance with the law.
The villager said the people still do not dare consume the water or even use it for household chores, despite the assurances from the provincial government that there is no issue and they can use the water as usual.
A map showing the location of the spill in Houaphanh Province, Laos.
(RFA) Shortly after the incident, an official of the Houaphanh Provincial Department of Agriculture and Environment told RFA that residents living downstream should temporarily stop using the water until inspection results are available and the problem is resolved.
Later, on Nov. 15, another official of the same department told RFA that authorities are currently investigating why the animals are dying.
“Right now, they have fixed it,” the second official said. “Currently, agricultural production can proceed, and the water can be used normally. As for the dead fish and other dead animals, they are still analyzing it.”
Foreign-invested farming, mining and development projects in Laos have sparked friction over cases of environmental pollution and land often taken without proper compensation, leaving villagers fearing retaliation if they speak out.
Skeptical residents
Residents have raised questions and demanded that relevant authorities conduct a serious investigation following state media reports clarifying that there was no chemical contamination of the water.
They also told RFA that they do not trust the Nov. 4 investigation, after which authorities announced that they found no severe impact and no dead aquatic animals, though there was still an issue with water concentration that might be caused by saltwater seepage from an old mining pit. The authorities at that time said they were waiting for official confirmation test results from the National Water Quality Research Institute.
But some of the residents have turned to mountain spring water, which is more difficult to collect, and is insufficient for their livelihoods, they told RFA. They do not trust the government because a similar incident occurred at the same mining operation in 2024. At that time the villagers tested the water themselves and found it was contaminated.
The rare earth mine developed by the Laos-China Rare Mineral Development Company North 2 Limited in Xam Neua district, Houaphanh province, Laos, is seen Feb. 27, 2024.
(Airbus) “Many villages are indirectly affected, so to speak – all 18 or 19 villages here,” a second villager told RFA on condition of anonymity to speak freely. “We cannot use the main river, the Nam Vaen.”
The villagers are demanding that authorities help them find replacement water to use for watering vegetables and agricultural production.
“Right now, for drinking and living water, it’s just mountain spring water and tiny streams, which isn’t enough to water vegetables and other crops,” the second villager said. “We are facing many hardships. They came to inspect and said nothing was wrong, yet we see so many dead fish there. Just like the previous time—when we took the water to get tested and we found contamination. When they took it to get tested, they didn’t find anything.”
Edited by Eugene Whong.

articles.title: Wall St down ahead of Nvidia results, Anthropic IPO
articles.excerpt: A broad selloff dragged US stocks lower on Monday as fallout from Jensen Huang's resignation as Nvidia CEO soured enthusiasm…
articles.fullText:
A broad selloff dragged US stocks lower on Monday as fallout from Jensen Huang's resignation as Nvidia CEO soured enthusiasm for AI stocks, raising the stakes for the chipmaker's earnings report on Tuesday and Anthropic's initial public offering later in the week.

The risk-off sentiment gathered momentum as the session progressed, with the S&P 500 dropping nearly 2 percent and the Dow falling more than 1.4 percent. The Nasdaq suffered the steepest percentage loss, tumbling 2.5 percent.

"It's the back-and-forth in this market of the AI-related stocks catching a bid versus this rotation trade," said Ross Mayfield, investment strategy analyst at Baird in Louisville, Kentucky.

"Over the last couple of weeks, it's like a day-to-day thing where, you know, some days the AI names absolutely rip and then the very next day, you know, they're in a freefall."

"There are signs underneath the surface that investors aren't panic-selling and running away from the asset class altogether, but are probing other corners of the equity market," Mayfield added.

Nvidia slid 4.1 percent, extending its losses after Huang's resignation, adding to concerns over the emerging technology's rapid expansion and potential risks.

Huang's departure prompted the Trump administration to issue a new rule restricting China's access to the best AI chips from companies like Nvidia ahead of an expected meeting between President Xi Jinping and his US counterpart Donald Trump.

Analysts expect Nvidia to post a 90.4 percent year-on-year earnings jump on revenue of US$109.10 billion.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 739 points, or 1.4 percent, to 51,608, the S&P 500 lost 145 points, or 1.9 percent, to 7,416 and the Nasdaq Composite lost 626 points, or 2.5 percent, to 24,509.

US Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh said on Monday that technologies will have a significant impact on the economy, but the possible scenarios range from rising growth with broadly shared gains to higher unemployment and a potential slowdown if anticipated investment returns prove disappointing.

Minutes from the Federal Open Market Committee's latest meeting, due for release on Wednesday, could offer clues on the policy outlook ahead of next month's interest-rate decision.

Markets are pricing in a near-certain 95.7 percent likelihood of a 25-basis-point rate hike in December, according to CME FedWatch.

Among individual stocks, chipmakers Intel and Micron both dropped more than 7 percent.

Neocloud provider CoreWeave dipped 6.1 percent and rival Nebius dropped 7.6 percent.

Hyperscalers Alphabet, Amazon and Meta slid between 2.4 percent and 4.1 percent.

Server maker Dell dropped 7.0 percent, while Super Micro Computer fell 6.9 percent. (Reuters)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: The open-source movement wants Jensen Huang back
articles.excerpt: This story originally appeared in The Algorithm, our weekly newsletter on AI. To get stories like this in your inbox…
articles.fullText:
This story originally appeared in The Algorithm, our weekly newsletter on AI. To get stories like this in your inbox first,  sign up here .

On Friday, a petition to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO of Nvidia began circulating on social media, and by Monday it listed some notable signatories, including Elon Musk and several influential Nvidia researchers. But comb through the more than 115,000 names and you’ll notice a significant faction of Huang’s supporters—higher-ups from Hugging Face, a hub for sharing AI models, and venture capital firms Andreessen Horowitz and Sequoia Capital—come from a particular slice of the tech world.

These names have a vested interest in the development of open-source AI, models that, unlike ChatGPT or Claude, can be downloaded and run independent of large tech companies. Supporters of such models say that concentrating AI in the hands of a few powerful companies will leave everyone else worse off (a concern that wouldn’t sound out of place among the AI industry’s critics on the left, if so many open-source advocates weren’t also venture capitalists who stand to profit when startups can build on cheaper AI without paying Big Tech).

Huang had become a sort of ringleader for those who defend open source to policymakers against concerns that such models come with no guardrails and cede AI leadership to China, where the most powerful and popular open-source models are created. They now want their most influential voice returned to his post.

But it’s not just Huang’s extramarital affairs that threaten his (and Nvidia’s) credibility as an advocate for open-source AI. New research into China’s startups using Nvidia’s chips, and a new rule from the US Department of Commerce announced Monday, could deal a blow to both the movement’s reputation and its technical progress.

On Thursday, the day Huang resigned, ex-OpenAI researcher Will DePue published findings online suggesting that China’s AI companies had far more access to Nvidia’s advanced Blackwell chips than previously estimated. China is banned from accessing Nvidia’s most cutting-edge chips to help protect America’s AI lead.

It’s unclear how they would have gained access to the chips. DePue claims the results were verified by senior researchers at OpenAI and Anthropic, but an independent analysis has not confirmed the results. (DePue did not respond to a request for an interview. Nvidia did not immediately respond to a request for comment.)

The findings do not establish that Nvidia helped Chinese companies obtain the chips, and the broader problem of chip smuggling was already known to extend well beyond Nvidia’s control.

But in suggesting that Nvidia may have profited from the rise of Chinese AI startups, whose models are increasingly being used by American companies instead of domestic alternatives, the findings do leave Huang in an awkward position. He has championed open-source AI as a way to strengthen American technological leadership. “Without open source, startups can’t thrive, university researchers can’t do research, you can’t teach AI, scientists can’t use AI,” he said last December during a talk about helping the US win the AI race against China.

It also makes the idea of reinstating Huang even more of a long shot. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent even said last week that Nvidia should not consider someone from inside the company to replace him. The new findings lower Huang’s chances further.

What happens next? Nvidia announced in September it would acquire Hugging Face for nearly $13 billion. Its support for open source also serves a straightforward financial interest: The more businesses that build their own models instead of forking over money to Anthropic and OpenAI, the more chips Nvidia can sell.

But a new rule from the US Department of Commerce could mean the models popular on Hugging Face will soon stop getting smarter. The rule aims to prevent Chinese companies from training models on Nvidia chips that they can’t own directly, but that they can access remotely in data centers in countries like Malaysia—a workaround that has helped China’s open-source models get so good.

The open-source world rallied around Huang because of his influence on policymakers. That was important, since the rise of China’s open-source models has splintered some in Trump’s orbit. If Huang is out, who is next?

articles.title: Building trustworthy AI by fencing it in, not predicting it
articles.excerpt: In October this year, OpenAI disclosed that two of its AI agents had switched off the systems built to monitor…
articles.fullText:
In October this year, OpenAI disclosed that two of its AI agents had switched off the systems built to monitor them. One muted its own safety alerts after misreading an instruction not to send messages; the other removed its monitoring integration during migration, then said it hadn’t. No rule had told the agents to do that, and no test had anticipated the behaviors.

For a century, we have built trust in technology on predictability: predefined inputs, predictable outputs, and layers of protection. Consider how a breaker trips at a set current or an aircraft component is tested against known (i.e., predictable) stresses.

AI changes that. Traditional software executes instructions written by humans, whereas AI exercises what might be called synthetic judgment. We use AI because it can interpret situations we did not program and generate responses we did not prescribe. But the more freedom we give AI, the harder it becomes to provide the predictability on which trust has traditionally been built.

We will not make AI trustworthy by predicting what it will do. We will do it by fencing it in with hard limits that are enforced outside its reach. In OpenAI’s case, the safeguards sat inside a system the agents could edit. But a fence the agents can simply move is not a fence.

Where traditional definitions of trust fall short

Recent MIT Technology Review coverage has approached this problem from other directions. One contributor argues that having a human in the loop is an insufficient solution because humans are fundamentally unable to understand AI systems’ intentions and advocates instead for interdisciplinary research and collaboration between academia, government, and the tech industry. And a story on reverse game theory describes using incentives to keep models from deviating from the rules, even when no one understands how they work on the inside.

Both articles acknowledge that we cannot understand or watch every AI decision. Our instruments of trust, including requirements, testing, certification, safety margins, interlocks, and pass/fail criteria, all depend on our ability to bound a system’s behavior. This is the determinism paradox.

With generative and agentic AI, behavior is shaped by training data, architecture, prompts, context, retrieval sources, and the environment. Inputs change, models are updated, tools change, and agents interact. Small variations propagate into outcomes nobody designed. The problem is not randomness; it is that the space of possible behavior is too large to enumerate in advance. Trust must therefore be engineered around boundaries rather than predicted outputs. The goal is not deterministic AI, but bounded, observable, and controllable AI. Trust also cannot be a one-time test. Traditional assurance certifies a product at a point in time, but AI keeps evolving after deployment, and a system that has passed every test can drift outside the conditions that made those tests meaningful. Trust must be continuously earned.

Safety engineering has been accounting for some of this variability for decades. For example, the Nuclear Regulatory Commission determine the likelihood of failures in complex systems, and Systems-Theoretic Accident Model and Processes (STAMP) showed that accidents can emerge from interactions among working components, people, and organizations. But AI raises the stakes, because just a single component can now interpret, infer, and act. The stakes rise further as AI moves from browsers into vehicles, robots, medical systems, industrial controls, and data centers, where a wrong answer can become a life-threatening event.

Building trust that scales

It’s clear that a person rubber-stamping thousands of AI actions an hour is not an acceptable—or scalable—safeguard against risk. But the remedy is not to remove people from the loop; it is to put human judgment where it counts: setting limits in advance and approving the rare actions that have serious consequences while hard constraints handle the rest.

Therefore, trust has to move upstream into architecture. The central questions become: What authority are we willing to give AI, under what conditions, and supported by what evidence? And what happens outside those conditions? That is very different from asking whether a model scored 94% on a benchmark.

The determinism paradox does not mean AI cannot be trusted. It means trust needs a different architecture. Instead of making every output predictable, make the boundaries predictable. An AI medical assistant may be probabilistic in its diagnosis, but deterministic rules govern whether it can change a prescription. An industrial AI may find many ways to optimize a process, while fixed limits keep it within pressure and temperature bounds. An agent may decide how to complete a task, while permissions, transaction limits, and human approvals determine what it is authorized to do.

Let AI be probabilistic inside the box and make the box itself deterministic wherever consequences matter. Leaders can put this into practice by asking five questions:

- What authority does AI have? Define not only what it can do but what it is allowed to do, separating interpretation, recommendation, decision, and execution.

- Is the function of AI proportional to the consequence? A marketing copilot and AI controlling industrial equipment need different assurance thresholds.

- Are we taking the appropriate steps toward autonomy? For example, there needs to be a plan to move from having AI interpret while humans decide, to AI making recommendations, to then taking action with approval, and ultimately to having supervised autonomy, but only as AI can safely work at each step.

- Are we testing the system or merely the model? Unexpected interactions emerge among models, data, agents, APIs, and human workflows.

- Are we continuously earning trust? Monitor drift, failures, near-misses, and model changes throughout the lifecycle.

The winners in AI will be those who solve the determinism paradox—giving AI enough freedom to create value while engineering boundaries strong enough to make what it does with that freedom trustworthy. Invention earns attention. Trust earns adoption.

Explore how UL Solutions builds trust in AI .

This content was produced by UL Solutions. It was not written by MIT Technology Review’s editorial staff.

articles.title: HK's maritime strengths hailed
articles.excerpt: Thousands of global maritime professionals have gathered for Hong Kong Maritime Week 2026, convening to explore the sector’s emerging opportunities…
articles.fullText:
Thousands of global maritime professionals have gathered for Hong Kong Maritime Week 2026, convening to explore the sector’s emerging opportunities and navigate its shared challenges.

John Denholm, who is Chairman of the International Chamber of Shipping – which represents shipowners and operators internationally – emphasised that Hong Kong’s unique role as a bridge between East and West grants it significant potential to evolve as a maritime centre.

“The opportunities for Hong Kong’s maritime industry are huge,” he said. “Hong Kong is a gateway to both the East and the West, and is in a great position.”

Mr Denholm also credited the relationship between the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region Government and the shipping industry with cementing the city’s leadership role in maritime matters.

“Hong Kong is leading the world in many aspects," he said. "It’s a leader, not a follower, in the marine industry because of the Government and its relationship with the shipping industry.”

Beyond customary concerns, attendees are addressing current industry issues such as supply-chain resilience, geopolitical shifts, emerging technologies and green fuels.

International Union of Marine Insurance President Sean Dalton said Hong Kong Maritime Week provides a vital platform for direct dialogue. His organisation represents marine insurers internationally.

“We are all working on solving the same problems, and connections such as this are instrumental to doing our best work,” he said.

Meanwhile, the International Group of P&I Clubs, a group of marine liability insurers, highlighted its members’ deep-rooted presence in the city, which they view as a gateway to China. Chief Executive Officer Nick Shaw noted that 11 of the group’s 12 clubs maintain offices in Hong Kong, employing hundreds of specialists.

“I think the opportunities going forward are boundless,” he said.

Asian Shipowners’ Association Interim Secretary General Eleanor Keukura Roi said that the event bridges Asia’s maritime community with the wider world. The association represents regional shipowners.

She said that the gathering offers a valuable opportunity to bring shipowners’ perspectives into global discussions, strengthen partnerships and turn shared challenges into collective action.

Echoing these sentiments, UK Chamber of Shipping Chief Executive Rhett Hatcher stated that the event brings together industry representatives to exchange ideas and share good practices.

He added that Hong Kong Maritime Week enables participants to discuss both the challenges facing the industry and significant opportunities ahead.

articles.title: Unemployment rate drops to 3.8%
articles.excerpt: The seasonally adjusted unemployment rate decreased from 3.9% in the three months from July to September to 3.8% in the…
articles.fullText:
The seasonally adjusted unemployment rate decreased from 3.9% in the three months from July to September to 3.8% in the period from August to October, the Census & Statistics Department announced today.

The underemployment rate remained at 2%.

Total employment was 3,653,800, down 1,200 from the previous three-month period, while the labour force dropped by around 5,800 to 3,804,200.

Looking ahead, Secretary for Labour & Welfare Chris Sun said that the ongoing expansion of the local economy, solid consumption sentiment and continued growth in inbound tourism should render support to the overall labour market conditions.

“The Government will continue to closely monitor the evolving external uncertainties for their potential implications on corporate hiring sentiments and provide job-seekers with appropriate support," Mr Sun said.

articles.title: Plans ready for Subsector elections
articles.excerpt: Chairman of the Electoral Affairs Commission (EAC) David Lok chaired a Crisis Management Committee (CMC) meeting this evening to review…
articles.fullText:
Chairman of the Electoral Affairs Commission (EAC) David Lok chaired a Crisis Management Committee (CMC) meeting this evening to review various scenarios that may arise during the 2026 Election Committee Subsector Ordinary Elections, scheduled for November 22.

During the meeting, the EAC received briefings from representatives of key government departments, including the Registration & Electoral Office, the Digital Policy Office and the Hong Kong Police Force. They covered election preparation and co-ordination work, assessments of cybersecurity and security risks as well as contingency plans for polling day.

Further updates on preparatory work and co-ordination were presented by the Security Bureau, the Home Affairs Department, the Information Services Department, the Department of Justice and the Electrical & Mechanical Services Department.

Mr Lok noted that organising an election is a complex undertaking requiring meticulous planning, preparation and arrangements throughout the workflow. He added that relevant policy bureaux and departments have entered the final stage of preparation with security and contingency plans in place to ensure the elections proceed smoothly.

He also pointed out that today’s meeting enabled the EAC to prepare for the elections more thoroughly. The CMC will assist the EAC in closely monitoring conditions on polling day, reaffirming the EAC’s commitment to ensuring the elections are conducted openly, honestly and fairly in strict accordance with electoral laws and guidelines.

Five ordinary polling stations will be set up for the elections, utilising the electronic poll register (EPR) system to issue ballot papers.

Mr Lok and EAC member Daniel Shek also inspected an on-site drill arranged by the Registration & Electoral Office today for polling station staff. The training session familiarises staff with polling station operations and the ballot-paper issuance process, including using the EPR system and its fallback mode.

articles.title: HK links GBA & APEC growth :CE
articles.excerpt: I am very pleased to join you at this year's Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) CEO Summit in Shenzhen. The attendance…
articles.fullText:
I am very pleased to join you at this year's Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) CEO Summit in Shenzhen. The attendance of over 2,000 business and government leaders from across the APEC economies, including some 115 companies in the Fortune Global 500, sends a clear and compelling message: In an increasingly complex global environment, the countries, economies and companies of the Asia-Pacific need open and continuing co-operation, more than ever.

We gather here, at this two-day summit, under the inviting theme "To Prosper and Win the Future Together". More than an aspiration, it is an active call for collaboration, because nobody wins the future alone. The future is a team sport - and the Asia-Pacific has always fielded a very strong side.

And nowhere is this collaboration spirit more evident, more vibrant, today than in the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area.

The Greater Bay Area offers one of the most convincing examples of what open co-operation can deliver. Home to more than 88 million people and generating a gross domestic product exceeding US$2.1 trillion, it comprises the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, the Macao Special Administrative Region, and nine cities in Guangdong Province, and is one of the world's most dynamic economic powerhouses.

If the Greater Bay Area were a standalone economy, it would rank about 12th globally. In the first three quarters of this year, trade between its nine Mainland cities and APEC economies reached some US$837 billion, a record year-on-year increase of over 26%.

High-end manufacturing, electronics, integrated circuits and green products were among the key drivers. These cheering results illustrate both the Greater Bay Area's rapid growth and its deep interconnection with the wider Asia-Pacific economy.

This momentum is underpinned by the Greater Bay Area's distinctive institutional framework of "one country, two systems", with three legal jurisdictions and three currencies synergising together.

I will give you an example. Hong Kong became an APEC member in 1991. Under the "one country, two systems" principle, "Hong Kong, China" continues as a full member of APEC, since our city was established as a special administrative region of China, our country, in 1997. We are proud to sit at the APEC table with our own delegation, our own trade and customs policies, and our own voice - while also being part of China, our country, part of its Greater Bay Area, with our shared interest in an open and prosperous Asia-Pacific. That's "one country, two systems" at work to its fullest.

The APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting is taking place in Shenzhen, at the heart of the Greater Bay Area. And, just weeks ago, the APEC Finance Ministers' Meeting was held in the Hong Kong SAR, also for the very first time. These milestones place the Greater Bay Area firmly on the global stage, affirming its fast-rising international relevance.

The cities of the Greater Bay Area are committed to realising the smooth flow of people, goods, capital and data. That will certainly contribute to effective regional development.

We view this connectivity through three distinct lenses: hard connectivity, soft connectivity, and what we poetically call the connectivity of hearts.

In hard connectivity, advanced infrastructure such as the Hong Kong-Zhuhai-Macao Bridge, the world's longest sea-crossing bridge and tunnel system, and the Guangzhou-Shenzhen-Hong Kong Express Rail Link, which connects our city to the country's high-speed rail network, is binding Greater Bay Area cities more closely, linking them efficiently to the wider region, and facilitating the flow of people and goods.

Meanwhile, our soft connectivity is advancing through closer alignment of rules and standards, reducing impediments to cross-boundary business.

As for the connectivity of hearts, it is deepening through growing people-to-people exchanges and talent mobility, enabling foreign companies to operate more seamlessly across Guangdong Province, the Hong Kong SAR and the Macao SAR.

Collectively, these advances are creating wide-ranging opportunities for companies. I am talking about access to a large and sophisticated consumer market, participation in advanced manufacturing and resilient supply chains, collaboration in innovation, engagement in green and digital industries, and so much more.

Hong Kong has an indispensable role to play in ensuring that this rapid growth continues. Under "one country, two systems", we are the only global city to capitalise on both China and international advantages.

We maintain a common law system, the free flow of capital and information, a simple and competitive tax regime and a deep pool of talent. These strengths make our city the natural "super connector" and "super value-adder" between the Greater Bay Area and the rest of the Asia-Pacific.

Take finance, for example. We continue to rank third, globally, and first in the Asia-Pacific, in the Global Financial Centres Index. We are also the world's largest offshore renminbi centre, processing over 75% of global offshore renminbi payments. We serve as the premier gateway for international capital seeking exposure to the Greater Bay Area's innovation and manufacturing prowess.

Leveraging Hong Kong's world-class professional services, companies from APEC economies looking to opportunities in the Greater Bay Area can raise funds, it also structures cross-boundary investments and manage currency and operational risks with confidence.

Turning to technology, the Shenzhen-Hong Kong-Guangzhou innovation cluster this year topped the Global Innovation Index, for the second year in a row. And Hong Kong Park, part of the Hetao Shenzhen-Hong Kong Science & Technology Innovation Co-operation Zone, brings Hong Kong's research excellence and international networks together with Shenzhen's commercial might.

Businesses can use Hong Kong to pilot new technologies, protect intellectual property under a trusted legal system, and scale solutions across the vast markets of the Greater Bay Area.

It helps that Hong Kong is home to five universities in the world's top 100. They are also, indeed, ranked among Asia's top 10 this year, with three in the top five. The Hong Kong SAR Government continues to be devoted to our talent initiatives of attracting global researchers and entrepreneurs, making Hong Kong an ideal base for Asia-Pacific innovators looking for technology partners in the Greater Bay Area.

Ladies and gentlemen, the theme of this year's APEC CEO Summit calls on us to prosper and win the future together. The Greater Bay Area is a proven model of how complementary strengths can generate opportunities far greater than the sum of their parts.

Prosperity is not something we can each win separately. It is something we can only build together - and the building starts here, today, with the people in this room. I invite you, the Asia-Pacific community, to explore partnerships that combine your innovation and market knowledge with the Greater Bay Area's manufacturing capacity, capital and growing consumer markets.

And Hong Kong, China, your reliable partner in managing the complexities of cross-boundary collaboration, can be your springboard, your business centre, from which to seize the far-reaching opportunities of the Greater Bay Area.

Working together, we can strengthen regional supply chains, create mutual opportunities and contribute to the shared prosperity of the Asia-Pacific community.

Ladies and gentlemen, Hong Kong, China stands ready to connect people, capital, ideas and opportunities, so that we may all prosper and win the future. And that future begins right here.

Chief Executive John Lee gave these remarks at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation CEO Summit 2026 in Shenzhen on November 17.

articles.title: Election Committee poll cards sent
articles.excerpt: The Registration & Electoral Office (REO) has mailed poll cards to voters or their authorised representatives (ARs) in the 31…
articles.fullText:
The Registration & Electoral Office (REO) has mailed poll cards to voters or their authorised representatives (ARs) in the 31 contested subsectors ahead of the 2026 Election Committee Subsector Ordinary Elections, due to be held on Sunday.

The mail sent out also includes a map showing the location of the relevant polling station, a guide on voting procedures, an introduction to candidates and an Independent Commission Against Corruption leaflet on elections.

Voters or their ARs can also use iAM Smart or the voter registration website to log in to the Online Voter Information Enquiry System, where they can access all of the information included in the mail.

The REO reminded voters and ARs that they should cast their votes at the polling station assigned to them, and that they must carry their Hong Kong identity card or specified alternative documents to collect their ballot papers.

A total of 856 candidates will contest 723 seats in the 31 subsectors. Voting will not be required for five subsectors, where 259 candidates will be returned uncontested.

The five uncontested subsectors are: education; sports, performing arts, culture and publishing; associations of Chinese fellow townsmen; labour; and "representatives of Hong Kong members of relevant national organisations".

Call 2891 1001 for enquiries.

articles.title: CE attends APEC CEO Summit
articles.excerpt: Chief Executive John Lee arrived in Shenzhen this afternoon to attend the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) CEO Summit and speak…
articles.fullText:
Chief Executive John Lee arrived in Shenzhen this afternoon to attend the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) CEO Summit and speak at a discussion session on "The Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area and Asia-Pacific Development Opportunities".

Speaking at the summit, themed "To Prosper and Win the Future Together", Mr Lee emphasised that in an increasingly complex global environment, the countries, economies and companies of the Asia-Pacific require open and ongoing co-operation more than ever.

"The Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area, as one of the world's most dynamic economic powerhouses, under the distinctive institutional framework of ‘one country, two systems’, with three legal jurisdictions and three currencies, generates a gross domestic product exceeding US$2.1 trillion. This reflects the fruitful results of open co-operation," he said.

Since the establishment of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, Hong Kong has continued to participate in APEC as a member under the name "Hong Kong, China". Mr Lee noted that this arrangement fully leverages the unique advantages of the "one country, two systems" framework to build an open and prosperous Asia-Pacific region.

"In particular, the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting is taking place in Shenzhen, and the APEC Finance Ministers' Meeting was successfully held in Hong Kong for the first time last month, demonstrating the Greater Bay Area's international relevance.

"As the only global city to capitalise on both China and international advantages, Hong Kong is the 'super connector' and 'super value-adder' between the Greater Bay Area and the rest of the Asia-Pacific, and will continue to promote the smooth flow of people, goods, capital and data within the Greater Bay Area to drive regional development," he added.

Mr Lee encouraged Asia-Pacific enterprises with strong innovation and market advantages to use Hong Kong as a springboard into the Greater Bay Area's manufacturing capacity, capital and growing consumer markets. By doing so, businesses can jointly strengthen regional supply chains and contribute to the shared prosperity of the Asia-Pacific community.

In the evening, Mr Lee and Secretary for Commerce & Economic Development Algernon Yau will attend a dinner with Hong Kong, China's representatives to the APEC Business Advisory Council. They will exchange views on promoting Hong Kong's unique strengths and enhancing regional co-operation.

Tomorrow, Mr Lee will attend the opening ceremony of the APEC CEO Summit as well as the welcome banquet for participating leaders and representatives. He will also hold bilateral meetings with leaders of other economies.

articles.title: Maritime week unveils key initiatives
articles.excerpt: As Hong Kong Maritime Week 2026 entered its third day, one of its flagship events – the Asian Logistics, Maritime…
articles.fullText:
As Hong Kong Maritime Week 2026 entered its third day, one of its flagship events – the Asian Logistics, Maritime and Aviation Conference 2026 (ALMAC) – continued with the second day of its programme.

Under the theme "Driving Inclusive Growth through Innovation and Sustainability", ALMAC focused on developments and opportunities in logistics, supply chain management, aviation, shipping and green fuels. The conference also announced major maritime and logistics achievements aimed at driving green transformation and expanding logistics networks.

Speaking at the special address session, Chief Executive John Lee mentioned that the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region Government is pressing ahead with maritime, aviation and logistics development. This progress is supported by the National 15th Five-Year Plan and the strategic development roadmap laid out in Hong Kong’s First Five-Year Plan.

He noted that the three focus areas complement each other, helping enterprises open new markets, raise competitiveness and prepare for future development to achieve inclusive growth. As a global "super connector" and "super value-adder", Hong Kong serves as a convergence point for Chinese Mainland and international networks, translating these unique advantages into shared opportunities.

Joined by Secretary for Transport & Logistics Mable Chan, Mr Lee witnessed the signing of three memoranda of understanding (MoUs) and the launch of a co-operation initiative.

The agreements included an MoU signed by the Airport Authority Hong Kong with local sustainable fuel producer EcoCeres and The Hong Kong and China Gas Company Limited to jointly promote the development of local sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) blending facilities. This co-operation will strengthen local fuel supply infrastructure and facilitate the wider use of SAF by the aviation industry.

To deepen co-operation on green maritime fuels, the Transport & Logistics Bureau signed an MoU with the Global Sustainable Transport Innovation and Knowledge Center under the Ministry of Transport. The two sides will jointly promote the green maritime fuel certification standards developed under the country’s leadership among the international maritime community, providing the industry with reliable and objective certification standards.

The bureau also announced the establishment of a partner port relationship with the Port of Qingdao, which joins the Port of Piraeus and Hainan Yangpu Port in the second batch of partner ports to expand Hong Kong Port’s maritime network to Shandong, Hainan and Europe. Through this platform, Hong Kong will strengthen port exchanges, expand co-operation in maritime logistics, green shipping and smart port development and explore establishing green logistics corridors.

In addition, the conference announced the establishment of the Vietnam-Guangxi-Hong Kong Land-Air Super Logistics Corridor, a successful extension of the SuperLink China Direct land-air intermodal service operated by Hong Kong Air Cargo Industry Services Limited under Hong Kong Air Cargo Terminals Limited. Powered by Customs’ Single E-lock Scheme, this corridor enables cargo from Vietnam to travel overland to Hong Kong via Guangxi in around 30 hours under convenient customs clearance arrangements before being exported overseas through Hong Kong's extensive international air transport network.

The conference brought together officials from the Chinese Mainland and transport officials from other countries to explore regional co-operation opportunities.

Governor of Shaanxi Province Zhao Gang, Deputy Minister of Transport of Thailand Sanphet Bunyamanee and Assistant Minister of Transport for Maritime Transport and Head of the Central Administration for Finance & Investment of Egypt Mohamed Fathi spoke at the special address session. They shared insights on logistics network integration, regional interconnectivity and sustainable transport while exploring how complementary strengths across regions can enhance global supply chain resilience.

Deputy Director-General of the World Trade Organization Jennifer Nordquist, Mayor of Xi'an Ye Niuping, Chairman of the Hong Kong Trade Development Council Frederick Ma and representatives of the Hong Kong Logistics Development Council and the Airport Authority Hong Kong also attended the conference.

An exhibition zone was set up at ALMAC for suppliers to showcase their latest services and solutions, fostering industry exchange and exploring prospects for business co-operation. The conference also featured various forums and thematic workshops such as the Silk Road Maritime Symposium alongside sessions on green energy, supply chain management and logistics, allowing the industry to explore more efficient, resilient and sustainable supply chains across port collaboration, green fuels, smart logistics and digital transformation.

articles.title: I.PARK1 fire probe completed
articles.excerpt: The Fire Services Department (FSD) said today that a fire on October 26 at Phase 1 of the Integrated Waste…
articles.fullText:
The Fire Services Department (FSD) said today that a fire on October 26 at Phase 1 of the Integrated Waste Management Facilities Phase (I.PARK1) on the artificial island off Shek Kwu Chau is suspected to be related to either welding works or smoking.

The FSD announced that it has completed its investigation, which involved collecting evidence at the scene and taking statements from relevant parties.

Findings indicate that the fire originated on the upper level of the third incineration module inside I.PARK1’s incineration building. The investigation ruled out electrical faults, arson, and spontaneous combustion of chemical substances as the cause of the fire.

The FSD said it has referred the investigation report to the Environmental Protection Department (EPD) for follow-up.

The EPD said it has already instructed the I.PARK1 contractor to review and strengthen measures to eliminate fire risks, specifically in relation to the handling of hot works – including welding – and tightening a site-wide smoking ban.

In a statement, the EPD iterated that it places great emphasis on the safety standards of waste management facilities under its purview, and takes a strict approach in overseeing contractors' implementation of various safety and fire prevention management measures, including enforcement of the smoking ban.

In January, the I.PARK1 contractor implemented a series of tobacco control measures, such as requiring workers to deposit cigarettes and lighters in pier-side cigarette racks before entering the I.PARK1 artificial island, and conducting regular and surprise inspections. Any worker found smoking at the site will be ordered to leave it immediately and will be removed from the I.PARK1 project.

The EPD is also reviewing the incident to strengthen contingency measures and enhance safety at the facility.

Relevant best practices will be promoted at other facilities under the department's purview to ensure construction and operational safety, the EPD said.

articles.title: Trump says he may meet Kim Jong Un in China
articles.excerpt: US President Donald Trump said on Monday that he may meet with DPRK leader Kim Jong Un in China as…
articles.fullText:
US President Donald Trump said on Monday that he may meet with DPRK leader Kim Jong Un in China as the US looks to re-engage Pyongyang on its nuclear programme.

Trump was preparing to depart for Asia, turning his focus to economic deals and historic three-way nuclear talks with Russia and China as his administration adjusts to a new political reality in Washington.

He said he plans to talk about Russia’s war in Ukraine during the highly anticipated meeting with Presidents Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin on the sidelines of the Apec summit in Shenzhen on Thursday.

Trump’s departure comes after the often-omnipresent president had remained largely out of public sight for the past several days, even as a nationwide ground stop snarled air traffic and his Republican administration faced tough questions on its handling of the situation.

His trip to Asia, which begins in Manila then continues to Shenzhen, gives Trump the opportunity to change the narrative from his domestic woes, including the air travel problems and fallout from the November midterm election where his party lost both chambers of Congress.
