The controversy over tech powerhouse and chipmaker Nvidia is also certain to hang over Trump’s visit to China, despite efforts by administration officials to downplay the president’s close ties to Jensen Huang, who resigned as CEO last week after admitting to an affair with an alleged Chinese government agent.

Beijing has said it was not involved and dismissed the spying allegations as "groundless".

Trump had no plans to raise the issue with Xi when the two leaders meet, said US officials who briefed reporters anonymously about the Asia trip under ground rules set by the White House.

Regarding Pyongyang, Trump met with Kim on three occasions during his first term but has not been able to get him to meaningfully engage since his return to the White House.

Trump has sought to set the groundwork for further talks with Kim. In August, he ordered the Pentagon to scale back joint military exercises with Seoul.

The three-way meeting in Shenzhen will also put in the spotlight the ongoing US war with Iran, which has been widely blamed for the Republican Party’s steep losses in the midterms. (AP)

Edited by Edmond Fong

articles.title: Xi on Zhongshan inspection tour
articles.excerpt: President Xi Jinping on Monday urged efforts to thoroughly study and implement the guiding principles of the fifth plenary session…
articles.fullText:
President Xi Jinping on Monday urged efforts to thoroughly study and implement the guiding principles of the fifth plenary session of the 20th Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee, and to strive to break new ground in the high-quality development of the Greater Bay Area.

Xi, who's also general secretary of the CPC Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, made the remarks during an inspection tour in Zhongshan, Guangdong province.

Stressing fully and faithfully implementing the decisions and arrangements made at the plenary session and leveraging new progress in persevering with full and rigorous Party self-governance, Xi urged a better job in advancing integrated development along the Pearl River Estuary, Xinhua News Agency reported.

Visiting an artificial island of the Shenzhen-Zhongshan Link, a sea-crossing project connecting the cities of Shenzhen, Zhongshan and Guangzhou, Xi demanded efforts to further enhance the management and operation of the mega transport project to better serve the development of the Greater Bay Area.

At an industrial park in Zhongshan, Xi learned about local efforts to absorb industrial transfers, transform and upgrade traditional industries, and develop emerging industries.

Building the Greater Bay Area is a major strategic plan made by the CPC Central Committee, Xi said, calling on cities along the Pearl River Estuary including Guangzhou, Shenzhen, Zhuhai, Dongguan and Zhongshan to play a pioneering role.

The president also visited the Museum of Dr. Sun Yat-sen and laid a floral basket before his bronze statue.

This year marks the 160th anniversary of Sun's birth.

During the inspection tour, Xi also stressed the need to continuously steer the economy toward innovation-driven and high-quality development, ensure that major targets and tasks for the year are fulfilled, and get the 15th Five-Year Plan off to a good start, Xinhua reported.

Edited by Edmond Fong

articles.title: Govt moves to implement Wang Fuk recommendations
articles.excerpt: Chief Secretary Eric Chan has urged government bureaux and departments to implement recommendations from the independent committee report on the…
articles.fullText:
Chief Secretary Eric Chan has urged government bureaux and departments to implement recommendations from the independent committee report on the deadly Wang Fuk Court fire “swiftly and precisely”.

This came as a steering committee led by Chan, which aimed at reviewing and driving forward the recommendations, held its first meeting on Monday to advance the coordination work for the reform of building maintenance and renovation system.

At the meeting, Chan urged the departments to roll out measures that are ready for implementation as soon as possible.

He said preparatory work for items involving legislative amendments must also be completed at full speed, so the amendments could be submitted to the legislature as soon as practicable.

The government said relevant bureaux and departments reviewed work plans, division of duties, as well as implementation proposals and timetables for pushing forward the recommendations during the meeting.

It added that the committee would hold meetings regularly to oversee the implementation of reforms and legislative amendment work.

Edited by Edmond Fong

articles.title: The Download: testing tech promises and searching for cognitive immortality
articles.excerpt: This is today’s edition of The Download, our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what’s going on in…
articles.fullText:
This is today’s edition of The Download , our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what’s going on in the world of technology.

Are we there yet? Six technologies that promised to change the world

How do you measure progress towards the future? In the Impossible issue of MIT Technology Review , our series “ Are we there yet? ” examines how far six potentially transformative technologies have come after years of promises.

We spoke to experts, researchers and engineers to find out what’s holding them back, then scored each on a progress meter from zero to ten.  Find out how we rated each of these technologies—and how close they are to delivering on their promise.

Nuclear-powered spaceships
Exercise in a pill
Interspecies communication
Solid-state batteries
Cleaning up PFAS
Eliminating traffic deaths

Subscribe now to get every issue of our print magazine as soon as it lands.

Inside the quest for cognitive immortality

Could technology keep your brain going beyond death? Far-thinking technologists are exploring ways to make it happen, from gradual brain replacement to uploading memories to the cloud. MIT Technology Review’s latest Roundtables event explores these ideas and how close they might be to reality.

Join science editor Mary Beth Griggs and senior editor for biomedicine Antonio Regalado for this subscriber-only discussion tomorrow.

Tune in live on Tuesday, November 17 at 5:00 p.m. GMT / 12:00 p.m. EST / 9:00 a.m. PST .

The must-reads

I’ve combed the internet to find you today’s most fun/important/scary/fascinating stories about technology.

1 Jensen Huang is considering a comeback as Nvidia CEO
He’s discussed with confidants the possibility of returning. ( FT $)
+ Elon Musk has joined 165,000 signatories calling for his recall. ( Guardian )
+ The Treasury Secretary wants them to hire an outsider. ( Axios )
+ ​​Megaspeed says the alleged China spy left the company last year. ( BBC )
+ Trump plans to name Nvidia an AI “national champion.” ( WSJ $)
+ Nvidia privately said it can track chips to China. ( MIT Technology Review )

2 SpaceX has caught a rocket returning from orbit for the first time
The feat brings fully reusable rockets closer to reality. ( Guardian )
+ The feat shows what audacious engineering can achieve. ( Atlantic $)
+ Meanwhile, Ukraine says SpaceX is lying about Starshield speed restrictions. ( Reuters $)

3 The US and allies have agreed to guard AI supply chains from China
Ten countries will collaborate to secure critical technologies. ( FT $)
+ Chinese AI stocks have plunged on export control fears. ( Information $)
+ Nvidia privately said it can track chips to China. ( MIT Technology Review )

4 The US flight shutdown exposed weaknesses in air traffic technology
Officials blamed the disruption on a faulty router installation. ( Reuters $)
+ It was a terrible week of outages. ( WP $)

5 The first in-body CRISPR treatment is set to reach patients next year
The treatment could gain FDA approval as early as March. ( Nature )
+ CRISPR has created female clones of male mice. ( MIT Technology Review )

6 Congress plans to make data centers pay billions more for power
A proposed bill would shift grid costs onto tech companies. ( NYT $)
+ Utilities also want tech giants to pay more for power. ( Bloomberg $)
+ Is data center hatred all about electricity? ( MIT Technology Review )

7 Apple plans to launch its first smart glasses next year
It’s betting on Siri to give the specs an edge. ( Verge )

8 Bill Gates has made billions from climate-polluting landfills
His investment in a landfill operator is worth $29 billion. ( ProPublica )

9 ​​A new AI device turns everyday objects into needy virtual pets
The tiny gadgets aim to encourage healthier everyday habits. ( Wired $)

10 Scientists made monkeys watch Minions to study their brains
Their findings challenge traditional vision models. ( 404 Media )

Quote of the day

“If our hopes for the future are pinned on any one individual being trustworthy, then we’re pretty screwed.”

—Helen Toner, former OpenAI board member, tells The Verge that AI needs stronger governance than trusting tech executives to do the right thing.

One more thing

How AI and Wikipedia have sent vulnerable languages into a doom spiral

When Kenneth Wehr started managing the Greenlandic-language version of Wikipedia, he discovered that almost every article had been written by people who didn’t speak the language.

A growing number of them had been copy-pasted into Wikipedia from machine translators—and were riddled with elementary mistakes. This is beginning to cause a wicked problem.

AI systems, from Google Translate to ChatGPT, learn new languages by scraping text from Wikipedia. This could push the most vulnerable languages on Earth toward the precipice.

Read the full story on what happens when AI gets trained on junk pages .

—Jacob Judah

We can still have nice things

A place for comfort, fun, and distraction to brighten up your day. (Got any ideas? Drop me a line .)

+ Adelaide Zoo is celebrating its first cassowary eggs in 34 years.
+ Photos fill the frame at the Epson Pano awards , which celebrate panoramic photography.
+ Indonesia has called an early halt to the world’s largest deforestation project , saving up to 4 million acres.
+ After over a month on the loose in Yellowstone, a little dog called Luna has been reunited with her owners.

articles.title: HK stocks firm as tech worries ripple through region
articles.excerpt: Mainland stocks ended lower on Monday, hovering near their lowest level since July 2025, dragged by hardware shares as worries…
articles.fullText:
Mainland stocks ended lower on Monday, hovering near their lowest level since July 2025, dragged by hardware shares as worries over the durability of the AI rally soured sentiment.

In Hong Kong, the benchmark Hang Seng Index ended 116 points, or 0.5 percent, higher to finish at 23,753 on turnover of HK$174.11 billion.

The tech index dropped 11 points, or 0.3 percent, to 3,801 while the China enterprises index climbed 44 points, or 0.6 percent, to 7,981.

New World Development fell 41 percent to close at HK$2.88 after the property developer proposed a HK$24.9 billion rights issue.

On the mainland, the Shanghai Composite Index ended 31 points, or 0.87 percent, at 3,602 on turnover of 706.21 billion yuan.

China's blue-chip CSI300 Index fell one percent.

The Shenzhen Component Index slumped 278 points, or 2.53 percent, at 10,690 on turnover of 778.27 billion yuan while the ChiNext Index plunged 106 points, or 4.37 percent, to 2,320 on turnover of 369.31 billion yuan.

The losses in Chinese AI hardware shares tracked their Asian peers, after a whiplash week capped by the shock exit of Jensen Huang as Nvidia chief executive, with the chipmaker's earnings and Anthropic's IPO this week set to test whether the AI-fuelled bull market can expand further.

The 5G Communication Index slumped 7.5 percent to its lowest level in a year, while the tech-focused Star50 Index tumbled 5.2 percent.

Zhongji Innolight, a leading maker of high-speed optical transceivers used in AI data centres, lost 12.3 percent.

The upheaval at Nvidia could prove a watershed for China's chipmakers, said Jeff Ko, chief analyst at ViaBTC.

"If Washington responds to the controversy with tighter export controls, it could accelerate investment in China domestic AI chips and computing infrastructure," he said.

China's economy showed fresh signs of sluggishness in October as factory production slowed and consumption remained weak, calling into question how long the world's second-largest economy can rely on exports to underpin growth.

"China's policy measures to combat deflation continue to be incremental and we remain below consensus for China EPS growth," Morgan Stanley analysts said in a note.

Valuations offer only partial compensation, they added, favouring stock-picking over broad market exposure.

In Tokyo, the Nikkei average slumped 1,480 points, or 2.4 percent, to 59,662, with Nvidia supplier Advantest and fellow chip equipment maker Tokyo Electron together contributing 1,072 points of the 225-strong index's net decline, with slides of 11.1 percent and 7.1 percent, respectively.

The broader Topix saw shallower losses, slipping 40 points, or 1.02 percent, to 3,901.

In Seoul, the Kospi closed down 190 points, or 3.59 percent, at 5,100 as one of its heavyweight constituents SK Hynix said it planned to spend US$1.05 billion over the next five years to support domestic suppliers of semiconductor materials, parts and equipment, aiming to strengthen its supply chain as competition intensifies in the AI chip market. (Agencies)

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Lawmaker supports decision to cut short harbour swim
articles.excerpt: Legislator Vincent Cheng, who took part in Sunday's cross-harbour swim, on Monday said it was appropriate for the organiser to…
articles.fullText:
Legislator Vincent Cheng, who took part in Sunday's cross-harbour swim, on Monday said it was appropriate for the organiser to call off the last race on safety grounds.

About 4,000 swimmers signed up to this year's annual race from Wan Chai to Tsim Sha Tsui.

Cheng said safety was the top priority and the conditions at the time posed a certain risk and the last-minute cancellation was a responsible decision of the organiser.

He said the currents were very strong during the final 300 metres to the finish, describing the situation as somewhat dangerous and chaotic.

"Normally a usual swim is probably maybe about 45 minutes, half an hour, but yesterday I swam for one hour 20 minutes, and I was still at the Avenue of Stars there, so there is also a certain risk there," Cheng told an RTHK programme on Monday.

He suggested that organisers should give participants earlier psychological preparation if they know the currents are strong, and consider extending the overall race time next time.

He also proposed refunding registration fees to those affected or giving them the opportunity to rejoin next year, as well as reviewing the race procedures and arrangements for better forecasting.

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: HKEX launches first offshore RMB bond index
articles.excerpt: Hong Kong Exchanges and Clearing (HKEX) launched its first index tracking offshore yuan bonds on Monday, providing investors with a…
articles.fullText:
Hong Kong Exchanges and Clearing (HKEX) launched its first index tracking offshore yuan bonds on Monday, providing investors with a new benchmark in a market that is central to Beijing's drive to promote the global use of the renminbi.

Financial Secretary Paul Chan described the launch as a milestone for Hong Kong's RMB market, giving investors a clear benchmark for measuring market performance and lays the foundation for index-linked products that will make these bonds easier to invest in.

"Like a landmark on a city's skyline, a good index gives a market a recognisable point of reference," Chan said.

"It shows at a glance where the market stands and how it is moving."

The index, developed by HKEX in collaboration with Bloomberg, tracks more than 300 offshore Renminbi bonds listed in the city.

Chan said the new index could set in motion a virtuous cycle, with funds and exchange-traded funds tracking it offering global investors convenient exposure to a diversified basket of RMB bonds.

Broader participation would lift secondary market trading, lower transaction costs, sharpen price discovery and ultimately reduce funding costs for issuers, he said.

Chan said the launch comes as RMB internationalisation enters a new phase, citing the launch of offshore mainland government bond futures in August and the acceptance of mainland government bonds as eligible non-cash collateral from this month.

He pointed to growing participation from overseas governments, corporates and multilateral development banks choosing Hong Kong to raise RMB funding, citing recent issuers from Indonesia and Kazakhstan.

He said this adds a new dimension to RMB internationalisation, with the currency becoming a funding currency for global issuers as well as an asset for international investors.

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Chinese output up 5.3pc on intelligent manufacturing
articles.excerpt: Value-added industrial output increased by 5.3 percent in the first 10 months on the mainland, according to official figures on…
articles.fullText:
Value-added industrial output increased by 5.3 percent in the first 10 months on the mainland, according to official figures on Monday.

High-end and intelligent manufacturing contributed to over 50 percent of output during the period, a National Bureau of Statistics spokesperson said.

For October alone, output grew 4.8 percent from a year earlier.

Robust demand for AI-related products and cars helped pull the Chinese economy out of a second-quarter slowdown.

With third-quarter GDP growth running at 4.5 percent year on year, analysts believe Beijing remains on target to reach 4.5 to five percent without the need for significant additional stimulus.

Trade data released last week showed that goods exports soared in October as the global AI infrastructure buildout continued to elevate sales of high-tech goods.

Total retail sales of goods and services, a gauge that measures goods consumption and catering revenue, increased by 2.5 percent year on year in the first 10 months of this year.

For October alone, retail sales edged up 0.4 percent after growing 1.1 percent the previous month.

Economists in a poll had expected a 0.8 percent increase.

Services retail sales grew 4.9 percent in the first 10 months, narrowing from five percent growth in the first three quarters.

There is huge potential for consumption but people's capacity and willingness to spend need to be enhanced, a bureau spokesperson said.

An AI-driven export boom has powered China's economic growth this year and looks set to shelter overall growth from external and domestic headwinds into 2027.

Fixed-asset investment dropped 8.1 percent in the first 10 months, compared to a 7.2 percent drop in the first nine months.

The surveyed urban unemployment rate in China fell to 5.1 percent in October from 5.2 percent in September.

New home prices declined again in October, albeit at the lowest annual rate in almost a year, extending a years-long slump that has eroded market confidence, sapped consumer spending and squeezed local government income.

Prices fell 0.1 percent versus September, when they also fell by the same percentage.

Beijing has in recent months introduced fresh support, including measures for steering cheaper credit into a range of sectors including infrastructure and technology, as well as expanding support for home buyers.

Regulators also in early November rolled out a handful of measures, from conducting swap operations to upgrading a lending facility for stock buybacks by listed companies, as part of efforts to stabilise struggling capital markets.

Looking ahead, policymakers will step up policy support for domestic demand if the tailwind from the AI boom tapers off, analysts said. (Xinhua/Reuters)

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Scotland fend off late fightback to beat Wallabies
articles.excerpt: Scotland survived a late rally to beat Australia 15-12 in the Nations Championship at Murrayfield on Sunday as the Wallabies…
articles.fullText:
Scotland survived a late rally to beat Australia 15-12 in the Nations Championship at Murrayfield on Sunday as the Wallabies suffered a fourth successive defeat.

The Dark Blues led 12-5 at half-time thanks to two tries from Matt Fagerson and Australia-born Jack Dempsey to one from Wallaby wing Harry Potter.

Neither side managed another point until fly-half Finn Russell's penalty six minutes from time put Scotland 10 points ahead.

But Max Jorgensen's 79th-minute try, converted by Ben Donaldson, gave the Wallabies hope of an improbable win before the recalled Scotland duo of Darcy Graham and Blair Kinghorn frustrated a last-ditch Australia attack.

Victory saw Scotland leapfrog Wales into fourth place in the Northern Hemisphere table.

Both teams arrived at Murrayfield with concerns over their defence.

Scotland lost 43-21 at home to New Zealand in their November opener last week, while the Wallabies went down 45-22 to England at Twickenham — the third match in a row where Australia had given up at least 40 points.

Scotland suffered a setback shortly before kick-off when captain Sione Tuipulotu pulled out because of a knee injury, with Tom Jordan taking the Australia-born centre's place in midfield.

Nevertheless, it took Scotland just eight minutes to open the scoring.

From a close-range scrum, the ball was worked to the onrushing Jordan and he found Ben White, with the scrum-half's pass releasing unguarded flanker Fagerson, who dived over out wide for his sixth Test try.

Finn Russell's conversion hit the post and just three minutes later Australia were level.

Scotland's defence was split apart as a delayed pass from recalled fly-half Carter Gordon and a missed tackle from Russell allowed Potter to slide over at a rainswept Murrayfield for a try Ryan Lonergan could not convert.

Scotland thought they had a second try when Kyle Steyn volleyed a bouncing ball forward from a grubber kick, with Darcy Graham touching down.

But the score was disallowed on review after Steyn was ruled to have been in touch.

But their second try did arrive in the 27th minute when back-row forward Dempsey — who won 14 caps for the Wallabies before changing allegiance in 2022— barged over with Russell adding the extras.

Australia then also had a try disallowed on review, with Billy Pollard's score from a driving maul ruled out for obstruction to leave Scotland 12-5 ahead at the break.

Pollard was yellow carded in the 46th minute for a head-on-head collision with Kinghorn but the Scots were unable to make the extra man count in a scrappy contest.

It was not until the 74th minute that Russell's penalty put Scotland two scores in front.

The Wallabies mounted a frantic rally which ended with Jorgensen speeding in for a try to give the hosts a scare before Scotland celebrated their fifth win in six Tests against Australia. (AFP)

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Andreeva defeats Svitolina to win WTA Finals
articles.excerpt: Russian teenager Mirra Andreeva battled past Elina Svitolina in straight sets to win the season-ending WTA Finals crown on Sunday…
articles.fullText:
Russian teenager Mirra Andreeva battled past Elina Svitolina in straight sets to win the season-ending WTA Finals crown on Sunday.

Andreeva powered to a 7-5, 6-3 victory in a hard-fought duel in Indian Wells to complete a superb week in California.

Reigning French Open champion Andreeva, 19, clinched the title without dropping a set in the tournament.

She is only the third teenager after Chris Evert and Maria Sharapova to win the WTA Finals on their debut.

"It feels amazing, of course I'm super-privileged to put my name in that group," said Andreeva.

The teenager thanked friends, family and support staff in a victory speech, before light-heartedly thanking herself for her success.

"I want to thank myself for always doing the hard work, for never quitting, for always believing in myself, for not taking the days off, for working every day, and for committing to what I have to do," said Andreeva, wearing a track-suit top with the slogan "I want to thank myself."

A grueling 1hr 48min duel saw Andreeva secure a break in the opening game of the first set before holding for a 2-0 lead.

Ukrainian veteran Svitolina broke back in the fourth game, conjuring a sublime angled volley to level at 2-2.

Svitolina was soon back under pressure though, conceding another break to go 4-3 down before Andreeva held for a 5-3 lead.

There was more drama to follow when Andreeva served for the first set at 5-4 up.

She opened with back-to-back double faults to go 0-30 down, and then yanked a wild forehand wide to give Svitolina two break points at 15-40.

A long forehand gave Svitolina the break to knot it at 5-5 but Andreeva hit back immediately with her third break of serve to regain the advantage at 6-5.

The Russian made no mistake when serving for the set for a second time, holding comfortably to go 1-0 up.

The second set followed a familiar pattern, with both players trading some brutal groundstrokes in a series of long rallies.

Andreeva broke to take the lead at 1-0 but Svitolina responded in a marathon second game, breaking back after converting her seventh break point to level at 1-1.

Andreeva edged back in front with a break to go 3-2 up and then held for a 4-2 lead.

The next two games went with serve to leave Svitolina serving to stay in the match at 5-3 down.

A fortunate net cord left Andreeva with three match points at 0-40.

Svitolina saved the first and looked poised to save another, only to hit a wide open overhead smash into the net to give Andreeva the win.

Svitolina, who had been thumped 6-4, 6-0 by Andreeva in the opening round-robin game of the tournament, took positives from her performance.

"After the first match I was not expecting to play in the final," Svitolina said. "Unfortunately it didn't go my way but I gave it my all." (AFP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: England topple world champions Spain in Nations League
articles.excerpt: England ended Spain's unbeaten run in competitive matches at 43 on Sunday, beating the world champions 3-2 on their own…
articles.fullText:
England ended Spain's unbeaten run in competitive matches at 43 on Sunday, beating the world champions 3-2 on their own patch, while Belgium thumped Italy 4-1 to join France in the Nations League quarter-finals.

Thomas Tuchel's team win Group A3, level on 15 points with Spain, after the hugely impressive win in Madrid in which La Roja were for long periods made to look a shadow of the team which won the World Cup.

But the Three Lions ended up down to 10 men and hanging on by their finger nails before inflicting on Spain a first defeat in a competitive fixture since March 2023.

Asked by ITV whether this was England's best performance of his reign as coach, Tuchel said: "Under the circumstances against who and where we played, yeah."

"(We showed) what we are made of and what we can do," added Tuchel, saying his team were motivated by their third place at the World Cup.

"We are always ready to push our limits. We had our best result in 60 years and we weren't happy with it. It's impressive what we did in the last two camps."

Harry Kane put the away side deservedly ahead on the stroke of half time, netting from the penalty spot, his record-extending 93rd England goal.

Ezri Konsa struck just after the break before Ben White gave England a barely-believable lead in the 57th minute when he latched onto Jude Bellingham's pass and finished between Unai Simon's legs.

England needed that cushion. Moments later they found themselves a man down when Elliot Anderson hauled backed Lamine Yamal in the box, conceding a penalty and a red card.

Mikel Oyarzabal slotted home the spot-kick with Spain's first shot on target to set up a grandstand finish and bring back memories of England's collapse against Argentina which cost them a place in the World Cup final.

Those jitters intensified when Nico Williams slammed home Lamine Yamal's inch-perfect cross with 15 minutes remaining, but England just about held out under a Spanish onslaught.

Sitting third in Group A1 ahead of kick-off and needing a win to qualify for the last eight, Belgium had their backs up against the wall when Francesco Pio Esposito volleyed Italy ahead in the 11th minute.

But Belgium blew Italy away in the following quarter of an hour, with Maxim De Cuyper and Nathan Ngoy bundling the hosts ahead before Jeremy Doku slalomed through the Azzurri defence and confidently shot home.

Mark van Bommel's team deservedly claimed a spot in the quarters and made sure the scoreline reflected the balance of play when one of many attacks against an open Italy defence ended with Diego Moreira slotting home with 10 minutes remaining.

A dismal night for Italy, who were top of the group after beating France last time out and just needed a draw to go through, was made even worse when Senne Lammens saved Esposito's weak late penalty.

"Nights like this can happen, unfortunately. These things can happen during a rebuilding process," said Italy boss Roberto Mancini.

"We're disappointed, but this is the kind of night that will ultimately prove useful to us."

France top the group after bouncing back from defeat to Italy with a 2-1 win over rock-bottom Türkiye in Bordeaux.

Les Bleus will head into the draw for the last eight, scheduled for Friday in Nyon, Switzerland, as a seeded team, a position that ensures they will host the return leg in March 2027 but could mean they face Spain.

An Emirhan Topcu own goal just after half-time and Eli Junior Kroupi's first goal for France were enough for Zinedine Zidane's team to prevail and take top spot in the final round of of matches. (AFP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: Building repair reform advanced
articles.excerpt: Led by the Chief Secretary Chan Kwok-ki, the steering committee set up to monitor the implementation of measures based on…
articles.fullText:
Led by the Chief Secretary Chan Kwok-ki, the steering committee set up to monitor the implementation of measures based on the recommendations of the independent committee in relation to the fire at Wang Fuk Court in Tai Po held its first meeting today.

Following the release of the independent committee’s report at the end of October, the Chief Executive announced that the Government would implement comprehensive and systemic reforms in relation to building maintenance and renovation, with oversight from a steering committee.

At today's meeting, Mr Chan directed bureaus and departments to implement the committee's various recommendations swiftly and precisely, with a view to achieving systemic improvements, streamlined processes, and effective implementation.

He emphasised that measures that are ready for implementation must be rolled out as soon as possible, while preparatory work for items requiring legislative amendments must be completed at full speed so that amendment proposals can be submitted to the Legislative Council for scrutiny and passage.

Relevant bureaus and departments scrutinised an in-depth review of work plans, division of duties, implementation proposals, and timetables for advancing the various recommendations.

The steering committee will keep the measures' implementation and delivery under review, enact reforms to every element of the building maintenance and renovation system, sever existing chains of interests, and take action to prevent similar incidents from recurring.

articles.title: Mainland uni applications to open
articles.excerpt: Candidates planning to enrol in the Scheme for Admission of Hong Kong Students to Mainland Higher Education Institutions can apply…
articles.fullText:
Candidates planning to enrol in the Scheme for Admission of Hong Kong Students to Mainland Higher Education Institutions can apply online from December 1 to 31, the Education Bureau said today.

The number of Chinese Mainland institutions participating in the scheme will increase to 169 for the 2027/28 academic year. Located in 21 provinces or municipalities and two autonomous regions, they will accept applications from candidates taking the Hong Kong Diploma of Secondary Education (HKDSE) Examination in 2027.

The Education Bureau encourages Hong Kong students to study on the Chinese Mainland via the scheme, thereby seizing opportunities to learn about the country’s social, economic and cultural landscape, and to bolster their own development.

The bureau said it will continue discussions to enable more renowned Mainland institutions to participate in the scheme, with a view to providing students with multiple higher education pathways and opportunities to connect with the country’s development.

Students should review their submitted application details online before January 10, 2027, while those providing supplementary information should do so before January 23. Students who pass the application verification process should pay the enrolment fee by January 31.

Institutions will announce admission results in late July next year. They may also arrange for supplementary enrolment depending on the enrolment situation.

articles.title: Australia down NZ to clinch Rugby League World Cup
articles.excerpt: Slick Australia overpowered New Zealand 32-12 in a pulsating battle on Sunday to lift a fourth consecutive Rugby League World…
articles.fullText:
Slick Australia overpowered New Zealand 32-12 in a pulsating battle on Sunday to lift a fourth consecutive Rugby League World Cup crown and reinforce their status as the sport's global powerhouse.

The home team took a 24-6 advantage into the break on a muggy evening at a sold-out Suncorp Stadium in Brisbane and never relented to inflict more pain on their arch-rivals.

Liam Martin and Jack Bostock bagged two tries each with Bradman Best and Tom Trbojevic also crossing in a fast and furious clash where Australia's fitness in draining conditions proved decisive.

The masterclass denied New Zealand their first title since 2008.

That upset – also in Brisbane – was the last time a team other than Australia lifted the silverware.

Since then the Kangaroos have won 23 games in a row at the tournament with Sunday's victory their 13th title from 17 World Cups played since its inception in 1954.

So dominant are they that they have lost just one of 20 Tests in the 2020s.

New Zealand performed an emotive haka, eager for revenge after going down 24-22 to Australia in an epic tournament opener over a month ago.

But they were immediately on the back foot, conceding after just 84 seconds.

Harry Grant threw a dummy and found big back-rower Martin who charged over with Cameron Munster adding the extras for a dream start.

After their shaky opening, the Kiwis knuckled down and after a sustained period of pressure centre Casey McLean stepped inside two Australian players to dot down and get them back in the contest.

Jamayne Isaako booted the conversion to move to 227 points, surpassing Shaun Johnson to become New Zealand's most prolific points scorer.

But Australia quickly restored order, with a beautiful offload from Best to Bostock in space who crossed in the corner.

Munster fluffed the conversion but made amends minutes later with a successful penalty to move Australia into a 12-6 lead.

The hosts were well on top and pierced a battered Kiwi defence again as Best finished under the posts before Martin collected his second just before the break with New Zealand tiring.

The second-half started where the first left off, with Australia's Trbojevic over after just four minutes, courtesy of Reece Walsh beating three defenders before the offload.

New Zealand were on the ropes with nothing going their way, including a try given by the referee then denied on review for a knock on.

But New Zealand persisted and Isaiah Papali'i split the defence for a converted try to leave them trailing 28-10 with 13 minutes remaining, only for Australia to hold firm with Bostock grabbing his second as the clock ticked down. (AFP)

Edited by Edmond Fong

articles.title: HZMB Half Marathon draws thousands of runners
articles.excerpt: Tens of thousands of runners – from professionals to enthusiastic amateurs – took part in the Hong Kong-Zhuhai-Macao Bridge Half…
articles.fullText:
Tens of thousands of runners – from professionals to enthusiastic amateurs – took part in the Hong Kong-Zhuhai-Macao Bridge Half Marathon on Sunday morning.

The event featured three groups: the 10-kilometre challenge, along with the half-marathon and open categories.

Secretary for Justice Paul Lam, who participated in the 2km Honorary Cup, said Hong Kong should host more major sporting events in future.

"[I am] very glad to have had the opportunity to run on the Hong Kong-Zhuhai-Macao Bridge this time. The weather was fantastic and the atmosphere was wonderful,” he said.

“This year's participation also set a new record, so I hope Hong Kong can host more large-scale sports events to showcase our strength, and I hope more members of the general public can take part in these activities."

This year’s event was upgraded to a World Athletics Platinum Label Road Race, marking the first time the city has hosted this level of competition.

Hong Kong, China's top female distance runner, Virginia Lo, said she was honoured to have competed with other world-class athletes.

“Having represented the city in various competitions over the past few years, I’ve actually seen first-hand how incredible they are, I hope I can keep improving and have even more chances to compete alongside them,” she said.

She also noted that the course was scenic and she was able to enjoy the sunrise at the start. But she also said it was quite sunny and windy, making it less than ideal for runners to perform at their best.

Edited by Edmond Fong

articles.title: Strong current forces organisers' hand in harbour swim
articles.excerpt: Thousands of swimmers took to the water for the annual cross-harbour race on Sunday morning, swimming a one-kilometre course from…
articles.fullText:
Thousands of swimmers took to the water for the annual cross-harbour race on Sunday morning, swimming a one-kilometre course from Wan Chai Golden Bauhinia Square Public Pier to the Avenue of Stars in Tsim Sha Tsui.

However, the race featuring one batch of contestants was cancelled due to strong currents, affecting about 700 participants.

The race drew a total of about 4,000 participants this year, with about 300 people participating in the racing group and 3,700 people registered to take part in the leisure group.

Keith Sin, the overall male champion, said the instructions of this year's race were clearer than last year's, with the navigation buoys ideally placed while the water temperature was comfortable to swim in.

"I have to say the organisers did a great job, while there might not be any obvious changes, those two navigation buoys were really well done," he said.

"They kept us from worrying about where the finish line was before getting in the water, since it's hard to see it from the starting point, navigation buoys are actually super important, so the organisers really nailed it."

The event also featured a leisure group with approximately 3,700 swimmers in four batches.

Ronnie Wong, president of the Hong Kong China Swimming Association, said although they were confident that all contestants could have finished, they decided to cancel the race for the final group due to safety concerns and time limitations.

"We made a decision today regarding the final batch of about 700 swimmers that due to water currents and safety concerns, we have cancelled the last group from racing, and we will refund their registration fees," he said.

Organisers said they would consider giving the affected swimmers priority registration if they want to take part in next year's race.

Organisers also said 135 contestants this year felt unwell, mainly suffering from minor abrasions and cramps.
